cases.SchemeSummary: Washington and co-conspirators stole personally identifiable information of Medicaid beneficiaries and used it to fraudulently obtain prescription medications from pharmacies across the Northeastern U.S., causing nearly $4 million in losses to New York Medicaid and tens of thousands of dollars to pharmacies; she agreed to forfeit over $400,000 in proceeds.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Massachusetts
cases.FraudEntity: Timothy Doyle (former operations manager)
cases.SchemeSummary: Doyle and managers of a mobile medical diagnostics company paid doctors cash and checks per transcranial doppler (TCD) brain scan ordered, disguising the per-test payments as fair-market-value rental and administrative services agreements; the medically unnecessary scans generated approximately $70.6 million in Medicare billings, of which Medicare paid about $27.2 million. Restitution of $27,225,434 plus $1,102,725 forfeiture ordered against Doyle.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Massachusetts
cases.FraudEntity: James Rausch (Northeast regional sales director for a mobile medical diagnostics company)
cases.SchemeSummary: Rausch and co-conspirators at a mobile medical diagnostics company paid doctors cash and checks based on the volume of transcranial doppler brain scans they ordered, disguising the per-test payments as fair-market-value space rental and administrative services agreements; the medically unnecessary TCD scans generated roughly $70.6 million in Medicare billings, of which Medicare paid about $27.2 million. Sentenced to 8 months plus $17,573,642 restitution, $408,437 forfeiture and a $20,000 fine.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of New Jersey
cases.FraudEntity: Jaekwan Lee (licensed physical therapist); co-conspirators including multiple health care providers and recruited Amtrak employees
cases.SchemeSummary: Lee, a licensed physical therapist, rented out his professional license and business bank accounts to conspirators who billed the Amtrak employee health plan for physical therapy services that were never provided and were medically unnecessary, in exchange for a share of the proceeds; other conspirators paid cash kickbacks to Amtrak employees for use of their personal and insurance information. The plan paid over $11 million overall to providers connected to the scheme (19 defendants, all pleaded guilty), including over $800,000 on claims tied to Lee.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of New York
cases.FraudEntity: Ali Rashan (medical doctor, CEO and founder of ClearMD LLC); ClearMD LLC
cases.PayerName: Medicare; Medicaid; HRSA COVID-19 Uninsured Program; private insurance providers
cases.SchemeSummary: Through COVID-19 testing clinics staffed by untrained 'medical assistants' rather than licensed clinicians, Rashan directed billing of Medicare, Medicaid, the HRSA Uninsured Program and private insurers for evaluation and management services and telehealth follow-ups that never occurred and for two to four COVID-19 testing codes when only a single test was administered, sometimes billing $5,000 per test; when payers requested supporting documentation, he had staff write software to generate fake progress notes and test results, causing over $24 million in losses.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Massachusetts
cases.FraudEntity: Juan Felipe Chalas; Efrain Rivera; Danis Piron Lara; Erpawi Roque Collado; John Doe aka Wilkin Emilio Pimental Pereyra; John Doe (true identity unknown, Hyde Park); Mercedes Soto Capellan; Oscar Gonzalez Melo; Cruz Augusta Pena Arias
cases.State_County: Massachusetts - Suffolk County (Boston, Dorchester, Hyde Park); Massachusetts - Essex County (Lawrence, Salem); Massachusetts - Bristol County (New Bedford); New Hampshire - Rockingham County (Salem)
cases.PayerName: MassHealth (Massachusetts Medicaid); SNAP (USDA); Social Security Administration
cases.SchemeSummary: Nine defendants, most unlawfully present in the U.S., allegedly used stolen identities (often of U.S. citizens from Puerto Rico) to obtain Massachusetts RMV credentials and U.S. passports, then used those identities to apply for and receive public benefits, including making false statements to obtain MassHealth health care coverage, SNAP and Social Security benefits, causing approximately $943,197 in total losses across all defendants ($776,715 of it MassHealth).

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of Texas
cases.FraudEntity: Tonya Crowder (pill mill clinic manager); Marlene Durham (pill mill clinic manager); Demetrius Onuaguluchi (pharmacist); Princepaul Agbonlahor (owner, Lahor Behavioral Services LLC); Nekewon Konah (counselor); Ginger Ruffin (counselor); Stephanie Harris (counselor); Takiya Caradine (counselor); Marizel Yukee (nurse practitioner, owner of four mobile wound clinics)
cases.State_County: Texas - Harris County (Houston); Texas - Fort Bend County (Missouri City); Texas - Montgomery County (Conroe/Humble); Texas - Brazoria County (Pearland); Texas - Fort Bend/Harris County (Katy); Nevada - Clark County (Las Vegas)
cases.SchemeSummary: Three sets of charges against nine defendants: (1) managers of two Houston pill mill clinics and a Conroe pharmacy allegedly issued prescriptions for over 3.4 million oxycodone, hydrocodone and carisoprodol pills and dispensed 136,000+ pills for cash; (2) the owner of Lahor Behavioral Services allegedly billed Texas Medicaid roughly $16 million for mental health services to minors that never occurred, with counselors creating fake visit notes and falsified timesheets; (3) a Las Vegas nurse practitioner operating four mobile wound clinics allegedly billed Medicare and TRICARE about $906 million (about $297 million paid) for medically unnecessary amniotic wound allografts applied to elderly and hospice patients, falsifying medical records and paying/soliciting kickbacks for referrals and allograft purchases.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Wyoming
cases.FraudEntity: Tera Marie Campbell (owner of The Olive Branch, LLC); Tayler Ann Krauss (medical biller/documentation assistant); The Olive Branch, LLC (behavioral health clinic)
cases.State_County: Wyoming - Cheyenne (Laramie County); North Dakota - Minot (Ward County)
cases.PayerName: Wyoming Medicaid; TRICARE; North Dakota Medicaid
cases.SchemeSummary: Campbell owned an autism behavioral health clinic in Cheyenne, WY and Minot, ND and, with her daughter Krauss as biller, submitted Medicaid and TRICARE claims for services never rendered (including on days the clinic was closed and while Campbell was abroad), for care delivered by untrained/uncertified staff supported by falsified certification and supervision records, and upcoded to higher-paying service codes. Restitution totals $735,717.63 to Wyoming Medicaid plus $135,890.91 to TRICARE across both defendants (Krauss jointly liable for up to $71,509.44 of the TRICARE amount); Campbell separately owes $225,000 to North Dakota Medicaid in a related case.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Louisiana
cases.FraudEntity: Zoe Marie Francis (chief operating officer, Institute of Women and Ethnic Studies)
cases.SchemeSummary: As COO of a New Orleans non-profit that received HHS grants and other federal funds, Francis embezzled organizational funds for personal events, Amazon purchases and family members, using falsified contracts and invoices to conceal the expenditures and granting herself unauthorized pay raises; she agreed to pay over $100,000 restitution and forfeit at least $150,000.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Louisiana
cases.FraudEntity: Zoe Marie Francis (chief operating officer, Institute of Women and Ethnic Studies)
cases.SchemeSummary: As COO of a New Orleans non-profit that received HHS grants and other federal funds, Francis embezzled roughly $150,000 by making unauthorized expenditures for personal events and Amazon purchases for herself and family, using falsified contracts and invoices to conceal the spending and granting herself unauthorized pay raises. She was sentenced to three years' probation with twelve months' home detention, and agreed to at least $100,000 restitution to the non-profit plus forfeiture of at least $150,000.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of California
cases.FraudEntity: Salud Para La Gente (nonprofit network of primary care clinics)
cases.State_County: California - Santa Cruz County; California - Monterey County
cases.SchemeSummary: Salud purchased misbranded Nexplanon contraceptive implants from an unlicensed wholesaler and administered them to Medicaid patients, then billed Medicaid for the drug and its administration using incorrect National Drug Code numbers to make the claims payable.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of Texas
cases.FraudEntity: Devin Jack Brodman (co-owner, Neva Diagnostics and Areahou Diagnostics); Kevin Darnell Curry (owner/operator, Acuity TMS); Dr. Olubayo Idowu (physician); Dr. James Lou Carlisle Jr. (physician); Vaughn Anthony Brozek (nurse practitioner); Catherine Nkeiru Maduka (owner/CEO, Saint Catherine's Hospice); Jason Charles Mareno; David Lee Lloyd; Jason Kashou; Duc Ngoc Ly a/k/a Michael Ly; Michael McMillan (owner, Protectus LLC); Neel Vivek Paithankar (owner, VMP Health Care LLC)
cases.State_County: Texas - Northern District of Texas (Frisco, DeSoto, Southlake, Hurst, Garland, Irving); Florida - Coconut Creek; Florida - Coral Springs; Mississippi - Meridian; Nevada - Las Vegas
cases.SchemeSummary: Thirteen defendants charged across seven separate Northern District of Texas cases totaling more than $365 million in fraudulent billing: two labs billed Medicare ~$65M for genetic/lab testing procured through kickbacks (Brodman); ~$26.9M billed to TRICARE for transcranial magnetic stimulation treatments not provided or medically unnecessary and induced by kickbacks (Curry); more than $25M in Medicare claims for medically unnecessary EEG testing ordered in exchange for kickbacks (Idowu, Carlisle, Brozek); over $3.1M in Medicare hospice claims for ineligible recruited patients and services never provided (Maduka); more than $73M in Medicare claims for unsolicited COVID-19 test kits shipped to beneficiaries, including deceased ones, with lab owners kicking back proceeds (Mareno, Lloyd, Kashou, Ly); ~$268M in claims for skin substitute wound care products with kickbacks to providers disguised as rebates/discounts, netting ~$174M (McMillan); and ~$2.3M in Medicare claims (3,700 claims, $1.2M paid) for unnecessary DME shipped after telemarketers posed as Medicare representatives (Paithankar). Over $35 million in cash, vehicles and other assets was seized.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of West Virginia
cases.FraudEntity: Muhammad Salman (pharmacist/provider); Bridgeport Pharmacy (his company); Jorge Roig (provider)
cases.State_County: West Virginia - Harrison County (Bridgeport); West Virginia - Brooke County (Weirton)
cases.SchemeSummary: Two West Virginia providers used pre-signed, invalid prescriptions issued outside the usual course of professional practice to patients while they were traveling and not near their West Virginia offices; Salman and his company Bridgeport Pharmacy also submitted Medicare and Medicaid claims for such services (paying $325,000), and Roig, who also collected controlled substances without proper registration or disposal records, paid $165,900.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Tennessee; U.S. Attorney's Office, Middle District of Tennessee; DOJ National Fraud Enforcement Division
cases.FraudEntity: Heather Marks (Advanced Registered Nurse Practitioner at Lifeforce Pain and Wellness); Lifeforce Pain and Wellness (pain clinic)
cases.SchemeSummary: Marks, a DEA-registered nurse practitioner at a small rural pain clinic in Carthage, Tennessee, prescribed nearly a million opioid pills (oxycodone, oxymorphone) to about 1,000 patients outside the usual course of professional practice, ignoring signs of illegal drug use and diversion; patients traveled hundreds of miles to obtain the prescriptions to abuse or resell. Convicted of conspiracy plus eight distribution counts; sentencing set for September 1, 2026.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Louisiana; Department of Justice, National Fraud Enforcement Division
cases.FraudEntity: Scharmaine Lawson Baker (licensed nurse practitioner and Medicare provider, independent contractor for telehealth company)
cases.SchemeSummary: A nurse practitioner working as an independent contractor for a purported telehealth company signed hundreds of orders for medically unnecessary cancer genetic tests after phone calls typically under 30 seconds and without examining patients (including ordering ovarian and cervical cancer tests for male patients), in exchange for kickbacks from the telehealth company; laboratories billed Medicare over $12.1 million and were reimbursed over $1.5 million.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Central District of California
cases.FraudEntity: Modern Nuclear Inc. (MNI) (La Habra-based mobile PET scan company)
cases.SchemeSummary: MNI allegedly paid referring cardiologists above-fair-market-value 'supervision' fees for PET scans - including paying for time the cardiologists spent in their own offices treating other patients or when off-site, and for services rarely or never provided - and then submitted the resulting referral-tainted PET scan claims to federal health care programs; resolved by an $8,334,350 FCA settlement plus future-revenue payments and a five-year corporate integrity agreement, following a qui tam suit.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Michigan
cases.FraudEntity: Orchard Laboratories Corporation (clinical reference laboratory)
cases.SchemeSummary: Orchard Laboratories, a participant in Medicare's over-the-counter COVID-19 test program, allegedly billed Medicare for OTC COVID tests that beneficiaries never requested and that were never delivered, collecting payment for undelivered kits between March 1 and May 11, 2023.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Michigan
cases.FraudEntity: Troy Sleep Center PLC; Care One Medical Equipment and Supplies, Inc.; Michel Alkhalil, M.D. (co-owner of TSC); Peggy Rahal, M.D. (co-owner of TSC, owner of Care One)
cases.PayerName: Federal health care programs; Michigan Medicaid
cases.SchemeSummary: Troy Sleep Center and its physician owners allegedly billed federal health care programs from Jan 2018 through Dec 2024 for sleep studies performed without properly trained and certified sleep technicians as federal regulations require, and obtained $480,000 in PPP loans while engaged in that billing; separately, Care One allegedly billed Michigan Medicaid (Jan 2018-May 2024) for PAP machine accessories that Medicaid does not allow to be billed separately from the machine rental rate. All defendants together agreed to pay $763,954.74 to resolve the qui tam False Claims Act allegations.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Middle District of Florida
cases.FraudEntity: Oasis Acupuncture LLC; Dr. Hui-Li Yuan (owner)
cases.PayerName: Department of Veterans Affairs, Veterans Health Administration
cases.SchemeSummary: Oasis Acupuncture and its owner allegedly submitted inflated claims to the VA for acupuncture needle reinsertion services that did not meet the required minimum of 15 minutes per reinsertion, causing the VA to overpay; resolved for $100,000 with no admission of liability.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Maryland
cases.FraudEntity: Valinda R. Nwadike, MD (OB/GYN physician)
cases.SchemeSummary: As part of a telemarketing scheme, the physician created and signed thousands of prescriptions for compounded creams and durable medical equipment such as knee braces after only a cursory phone call, without physically examining patients or reviewing medical histories; Medicare and TRICARE paid for the resulting medically unnecessary items.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Department of Justice, Civil Division and U.S. Attorney's Office, Middle District of Florida
cases.FraudEntity: Oglethorpe Inc. (operator of psychiatric hospitals); Robert Cohen (founder and principal owner); John Picciano (CEO); James O'Shea (Chief Operating Officer)
cases.SchemeSummary: Oglethorpe and its executives allegedly failed to return Medicare overpayments that their own consultants had identified for beneficiaries admitted as inpatients to two Ohio behavioral hospitals (Ridgeview and Georgetown) and a substance abuse clinic (The Woods at Parkside) who did not qualify for inpatient psychiatric care; the $32 million settlement is joint across the company and three executives, who also accepted a 10-year voluntary exclusion from federal health care programs after violating a 2021 Corporate Integrity Agreement.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of Ohio
cases.FraudEntity: Lonnie White; Lisa Ogletree (spouse)
cases.State_County: Ohio - Cuyahoga County (Cleveland); Ohio - Lake County (Willoughby Hills)
cases.SchemeSummary: White and Ogletree bought houses on Cleveland's east side, transferred them to nominal owners with fake renters, insured them for hundreds of thousands of dollars, arranged for the houses to be set on fire so the fires appeared accidental, and submitted fraudulent property insurance claims; nominal owners passed the payouts back to the couple, who moved the funds through other bank accounts. At least six fires and more than $2.3 million in fraudulent claims; White received 53 months and $2,375,861 restitution, Ogletree received probation and home confinement.  Not a health care payer case.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of Ohio
cases.FraudEntity: Timothy Sutton (licensed medical doctor, North Ridgeville, Ohio)
cases.SchemeSummary: Sutton, working for two Florida telemedicine companies, digitally signed pre-completed orders for durable medical equipment (braces) and cancer genetic testing, falsely affirming he had examined the patients via telemedicine and was their treating physician when he never examined any of them; the signed orders were forwarded or sold to other medical businesses that billed Medicare more than $14.5 million.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Western District of Oklahoma
cases.FraudEntity: Natasha Allmon (behavioral health counseling provider)
cases.SchemeSummary: Allmon, who had an agreement with BCBS to provide behavioral health counseling, submitted thousands of false claims for 60-minute psychiatric sessions purportedly given to her own family members nearly every day of the year, at times billing more than 24 hours of treatment in a single day, collecting about $1.1 million on $1.4 million in claims.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Florida; Department of Justice, Criminal Division, Fraud Section; U.S. Attorney's Office, Middle District of Florida
cases.FraudEntity: Mark Loftis (chiropractor and owner of Back Pain Home Supplies LLC, d/b/a EZ Medical Supply); Back Pain Home Supplies LLC d/b/a EZ Medical Supply
cases.PayerName: Medicare; TRICARE; CHAMPVA; HHS Provider Relief Fund (CARES Act)
cases.SchemeSummary: Loftis allegedly paid kickbacks to marketers for Medicare patient referrals and to marketers/telemedicine companies for signed doctors' orders issued without meaningful patient evaluation, then used those orders to bill Medicare, TRICARE and CHAMPVA roughly $30 million (about $8 million paid) for medically unnecessary orthotic braces and other DME that was not provided as billed; he also allegedly kept over $133,000 in COVID-19 Provider Relief Fund money by falsely attesting to its use and spent it on the DME scheme and personal expenses.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Western District of Virginia
cases.FraudEntity: Obioma Alozie Ndubuka a.k.a. 'Bank Roll' (co-conspirator/distributor); Kenechukwu Brian Okwara a.k.a. 'Kene' (co-conspirator, sold 'slots' with the doctor); Dr. Rotimi Iluyomade (Annandale-based physician, Crossover Medical Center); Cameron Isaiah Lewis; Elhadj Malick Diallo; Zion Oluwademilade Adeduwon; Yared Michael Tesfaye a.k.a. 'Yar'; Raymono Alfonzo Russel II
cases.State_County: Virginia - Annandale (Fairfax County); Virginia - Roanoke, Radford, Tazewell, Floyd and Honaker (Russell County); Maryland; California; Colorado; Nebraska; Arizona; Missouri; Florida; Pennsylvania; New Jersey; Delaware; Rhode Island; Georgia; Wisconsin; Texas; West Virginia
cases.SchemeSummary: A physician at an Annandale, Va. clinic wrote fraudulent prescriptions for oxycodone, hydrocodone-chlorpheniramine ('Tussionex') and promethazine-codeine ('lean') for fictitious patients supplied on lists by co-conspirators using fake names, name variations and false addresses (134 prescriptions under variants of the 'Ndubuka' surname, 56 addresses but one shared phone number); the prescriptions were transmitted to pharmacies in many states, picked up by conspirators who paid roughly $300 per prescription, and the drugs resold for profit, including via social media. Figures span multiple defendants: Ndubuka sentenced to 24 months, Adeduwon to 42 months, Okwara pleaded guilty, others charged.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Kentucky
cases.FraudEntity: Recovery Center of Kentucky, LLC; Recovery Center of Ohio, LLC; Recovery Center of Maryland, LLC; Recovery Center of USA (parent company); Dr. Warrick Stewart (CEO)
cases.State_County: Kentucky - Elizabethtown, Lexington, Louisville, Radcliff; Ohio - Cincinnati
cases.SchemeSummary: Operators of the Aspire Day Program billed Kentucky and Ohio Medicaid for children's non-covered education, recreation and lunch break time as if it were behavioral health day treatment, and Recovery Center of Kentucky misrepresented clinician credentials, billing services delivered by lower-level or unqualified staff as if provided by higher-licensed professionals to obtain higher reimbursement. Resolved by a $15,248,240.66 civil judgment against all defendants plus a five-year Corporate Integrity Agreement.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Department of Justice, Criminal Division Fraud Section; U.S. Attorney's Office, District of New Jersey; U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Vermont (federal court in Newark, New Jersey)
cases.FraudEntity: Purdue Pharma LP (opioid manufacturer)
cases.SchemeSummary: Purdue marketed opioid products to hundreds of prescribers it had reason to believe were prescribing without a legitimate medical purpose, and defrauded the DEA by misrepresenting the effectiveness of its anti-diversion programs and using prescriptions written by problematic prescribers to justify requests to increase manufacturing quotas; it also paid kickbacks to prescribers via its doctor speaker program and to an electronic health record platform to induce more opioid prescriptions. Sentenced to a $3.544 billion criminal fine plus $2 billion forfeiture (up to $1.775 billion creditable if it emerges from bankruptcy as a public benefit company).

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Central District of California
cases.FraudEntity: Israel Claustro (Orange County Superior Court judge; former Orange County prosecutor; operator of Liberty Medical Group Inc.); Liberty Medical Group Inc. (Rancho Cucamonga medical corporation); Dr. Kevin Tien Do (suspended physician employee)
cases.State_County: California - Orange County (Santa Ana); California - San Bernardino County (Rancho Cucamonga)
cases.PayerName: California workers' compensation program - Subsequent Injuries Benefits Trust Fund (SIBTF)
cases.SchemeSummary: Claustro, a non-physician, operated Liberty Medical Group and paid Dr. Kevin Tien Do more than $300,000 to prepare medical evaluations, record reviews and med-legal reports after Do had been suspended from California's workers' compensation program due to a prior health care fraud conviction; Liberty mailed the reports to California's SIBTF with other doctors' names listed on the billing forms and reports to conceal Do's authorship, resulting in approximately $38,670 in payments tied to Claustro's conduct. Do separately pleaded guilty in January 2025 to conspiracy to commit mail fraud and filing a false tax return.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Central District of California
cases.FraudEntity: Paul Richard Randall (organizer); Kyrollos Mekail; Patricia Anderson (prescriber); Monte Vista Pharmacy
cases.State_County: California - Orange County; California - Los Angeles County; California - Riverside County (Moreno Valley)
cases.SchemeSummary: Through Monte Vista Pharmacy, Randall and co-schemers exploited Medi-Cal's temporary suspension of prior-authorization requirements to bill tens of millions per month for 19 high-reimbursement, non-contracted generic drugs (including over-the-counter Folite vitamin tablets) that were medically unnecessary and frequently never dispensed; prescriptions were written by Anderson and procured via kickbacks, with proceeds laundered through a third party. Monte Vista billed over $269 million and was paid over $178 million; Randall pleaded guilty, Mekail pleaded guilty in Aug 2024, and Anderson remains charged.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Public Affairs; U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Oregon
cases.FraudEntity: Marie Gertrude Jean Valmont (owner/operator of Velida's Home Care); Yolandita Marie Andre (owner/operator of Velida's Home Care)
cases.PayerName: Medicaid (Oregon); Oregon Department of Human Services
cases.SchemeSummary: Mother and daughter operating an adult foster care home allegedly obtained Medicaid/ODHS 'exceptional payments' for extra caregiver hours for residents with exceptional care needs while paying the three trafficked Haitian caregivers little or nothing, lied about the victims' residence in the home, and Valmont falsified a disability claim so Andre could bill hourly as her Homecare Worker, including for periods when Andre was not actually providing care.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Middle District of Florida
cases.FraudEntity: Santiago Humberto Erazo-Zelaya (shell company owner/operator); Gregorio Jose Fuentes-Zelaya (co-defendant)
cases.State_County: Florida - Orlando (Orange County); various Florida counties (construction project sites)
cases.PayerName: Unnamed workers' compensation insurance company; IRS (payroll taxes)
cases.SchemeSummary: Erazo-Zelaya set up a shell construction company and bought a workers' compensation policy covering a minimal $100,800 payroll, then 'rented' certificates of insurance to work crews so contractors would believe the crews were insured employees of the shell company; contractors' payroll checks (approx. $3 million) were cashed by the conspirators, who kept about 6% (approx. $181,500) and paid no payroll taxes (approx. $765,000 owed to the IRS), and the insurer also paid a $26,720 workers' compensation claim. Figures span both co-defendants: Erazo-Zelaya received 14 months plus $765,446 IRS restitution, $26,720.12 insurer restitution and a $181,529 money judgment; Fuentes-Zelaya was previously sentenced to 33 months.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of North Carolina
cases.FraudEntity: Keke Komeko Johnson (compliance officer, Life Touch, LLC); Francine Sims Super (Kinston office manager); Kimberly Mable Sims (owner, 1 Choice Healthcare Services); Brandon Eugene Sims (owner, Life Touch, LLC); Life Touch, LLC (substance abuse facility); 1 Choice Healthcare Services (urine drug screening company)
cases.State_County: North Carolina - Lenoir County (Kinston); North Carolina - Wayne County (Goldsboro)
cases.SchemeSummary: Operators of Life Touch, LLC, a purported substance abuse facility, paid over $1 million in gift-card kickbacks to Medicaid beneficiaries who were drug users to induce them to appear for costly substance abuse counseling and urine drug screening services, which were billed to North Carolina Medicaid by Life Touch and affiliated lab 1 Choice Healthcare Services (including fake lab services ordered by Life Touch), totaling more than $12.7 million in billings; the defendants also lied and falsified documents during Managed Care Organization (Eastpointe) audits and a Medicaid Investigations Division civil probe to conceal the kickbacks, and failed to file/pay taxes on the proceeds. Figures span four individual defendants and the corporate defendant: restitution and IRS amounts across defendants plus a $15 million corporate fine, with over $6 million in cash, vehicles and real estate seized/forfeited.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of New Jersey
cases.FraudEntity: Stephen Corba (owner of wholesale drug distributor); Frank Incognito (operations manager); Anise Kachadourian (doctor); Jon Paul Dadaian (doctor); Joel Lerner (doctor)
cases.State_County: New Jersey - Middlesex County (Sewaren); New Jersey - Monmouth County (Englishtown, Farmingdale)
cases.SchemeSummary: Corba and Incognito, who ran a wholesale drug distributor, conspired with physicians to 'straw-purchase' expensive cold-chain biologic oncology and ophthalmology infusion drugs from pharmaceutical manufacturers and authorized distributors using the doctors' medical licenses, falsely representing the drugs would treat the doctors' own patients and would not be resold; the drugs were instead diverted and resold to the distributor's customers for profit, totaling more than $47.5 million in drugs over June 2012-January 2019. Three doctors also pleaded guilty; sentencing for Corba and Incognito is pending, with restitution agreed for the full loss amount.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of Illinois
cases.FraudEntity: Hassan Abdellatif (owner of several Chicago-area convenience stores); eight other convenience store owners or workers (charged, pleaded guilty)
cases.PayerName: USDA Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) program
cases.SchemeSummary: Abdellatif and eight co-schemers who owned or worked at Chicago-area convenience stores let customers use federally funded WIC checks to pay for items not covered by the program, often at inflated prices, and then redeemed those checks for reimbursement; ten stores in the scheme redeemed over $19 million in WIC checks. Abdellatif was convicted at trial on wire fraud, fraudulently obtaining government benefits, and failing to file corporate tax returns, and was sentenced to 48 months plus $8.8 million restitution; the eight co-defendants pleaded guilty and await sentencing.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Wisconsin
cases.FraudEntity: Precious Cruse (owner of defunct prenatal care coordination company)
cases.SchemeSummary: Cruse, through her prenatal care coordination company, billed a Wisconsin Medicaid benefit intended for at-risk pregnant women and women with young children, stealing $780,600.07; a jury convicted her of nine counts of health care fraud, two counts of false statements relating to health care matters, two anti-kickback violations, money laundering, and two counts of aggravated identity theft (indicating use of patient identities and kickbacks to obtain claims payments).

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of Texas; Justice Department Criminal Division, Fraud Section
cases.FraudEntity: Patrick Cassells (owner/operator of three durable medical equipment companies)
cases.State_County: Texas - Fort Bend County (Fulshear); Texas - Harris County (Houston)
cases.SchemeSummary: Cassells owned three DME companies (hiding his ownership of one by naming a straw owner on the Medicare enrollment application) and paid kickbacks, disguised as payments for 'leads' and 'marketing,' to co-conspirators who supplied signed doctors' orders for orthotic braces issued without any patient examination; he then billed Medicare over $59.9 million falsely certifying the braces as medically necessary, collecting over $27 million.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Florida; U.S. Department of Justice, Criminal Division Fraud Section / National Fraud Enforcement Division and U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of Florida
cases.FraudEntity: Brett Blackman (founder, owner and CEO of HealthSplash); HealthSplash; Power Mobility Doctor Rx, LLC (DMERx); Gary Cox (co-defendant)
cases.State_County: Florida (Southern District of Florida); Kansas - Johnson County (defendant's residence)
cases.PayerName: Medicare; other federal health care benefit programs (military/TRICARE and VA programs referenced); other insurers
cases.SchemeSummary: Blackman owned the DMERx internet platform, which generated false doctors' orders and prescriptions for orthotic braces, other DME and pharmacy items; foreign call centers and spam mailers recruited hundreds of thousands of Medicare beneficiaries, and telemedicine doctors were paid kickbacks to sign orders falsely stating they had examined and tested patients they often never spoke to, while DME suppliers and pharmacies paying kickbacks for the orders billed Medicare and other programs over $1 billion and were paid more than $450 million; the scheme was hidden via sham contracts and order manipulation to evade audits. Co-defendant Gary Cox was convicted in a prior trial and sentenced to 15 years; Blackman awaits sentencing on Aug. 26, 2026.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of New York
cases.FraudEntity: Adnan Arshad, a/k/a 'Eddie' (owner of MTK Taxi LLC and co-owner of All-Star Taxi LLC); at least five unnamed co-conspirators who pleaded guilty
cases.State_County: New York - Suffolk County (Montauk, Ronkonkoma, Mount Sinai), Long Island; New York City
cases.SchemeSummary: Arshad, who owned/co-owned Long Island ambulette/taxi companies, paid kickbacks to Medicaid beneficiaries to order medical transportation (purportedly to methadone/addiction treatment) through his companies, then billed Medicaid over $19 million for rides that were never provided, including for beneficiaries who were deceased, hospitalized or incarcerated; he also inflated reimbursements by directing beneficiaries to distant New York City clinics and to give false pickup addresses to make trips appear longer, billing over $16 million for trips to three NYC treatment centers, and laundered proceeds into homes and luxury vehicles. At least five co-conspirators have pleaded guilty and await sentencing.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Wisconsin
cases.FraudEntity: Markita Barnes (owner of a now-closed Milwaukee prenatal care coordination company)
cases.SchemeSummary: Barnes, who owned a Milwaukee prenatal care coordination company, billed a Wisconsin Medicaid benefit program intended for at-risk pregnant women and women with young children, stealing $2,361,799.17; a jury convicted her of ten counts of health care fraud, three counts of false statements in health care matters, three anti-kickback violations, obstruction of a health care fraud investigation, money laundering, and two counts of aggravated identity theft.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Wisconsin
cases.FraudEntity: Lakia Jackson (owner of now-closed Milwaukee prenatal care coordination company)
cases.SchemeSummary: Jackson, who ran a Milwaukee prenatal care coordination company, paid women kickbacks in exchange for their Medicaid numbers and then billed Wisconsin Medicaid's prenatal care coordination benefit at nearly the maximum amount permitted per month per beneficiary, while she and her employees provided few or no covered services, stealing $2,655,463.63.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of Florida; Justice Department Criminal Division, Fraud Section
cases.FraudEntity: Patrick Boyd (owner and Managing Partner, Safe Chain Solutions); Charles Boyd (owner and CEO, Safe Chain Solutions); Safe Chain Solutions (wholesale pharmaceutical distributor); Adam Brosius (co-conspirator)
cases.State_County: Maryland; Florida - Southern District of Florida
cases.SchemeSummary: The Boyd brothers, through wholesale distributor Safe Chain Solutions, bought more than 28,000 bottles of HIV medication diverted from patients via black-market 'buyback' suppliers (labels removed, bottles dirty/unsealed, sometimes shipped in scavenged boxes), then resold them to pharmacies with falsified pedigree paperwork so the drugs re-entered the legitimate supply chain; Medicare, Medicaid and commercial insurers were billed and paid for these illicit drugs. They paid over $92.8 million for the drugs; Patrick Boyd received 18 years, Charles Boyd 20 years, co-defendant Adam Brosius 97 months, and the Boyds were ordered to forfeit $21,850,000.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Middle District of Pennsylvania
cases.FraudEntity: PA Lifesharing, LLC (provider); Carolyn Bennett Carson; Rajkumar Wale
cases.SchemeSummary: PA Lifesharing billed Pennsylvania Medicaid for 1:1 direct support services rendered by Direct Support Professionals whom it knew were not properly cleared and/or trained, making them unqualified under Medicaid rules; resolved via a $1,211,095.53 FCA settlement arising from a qui tam suit, with $242,219 to the whistleblower.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Western District of Virginia
cases.FraudEntity: John Gregory 'Greg' Barnes (owner of pain clinics); L5 Medical Holdings (corporate entity); Jennifer Adams (chief operating officer); Duane Dixon (doctor); Charles Wilson Adams (falsely held out as a doctor); Wendell Randall (doctor); Debra Shaffer (nurse practitioner)
cases.State_County: Virginia - Lynchburg; Virginia - Madison Heights (Amherst County); Virginia - Christiansburg (Montgomery County); Virginia - Woodlawn (Carroll County)
cases.SchemeSummary: Barnes, with no medical training, bought and ran L5 pain clinics that prioritized revenue over care: non-medical staff made prescribing/treatment decisions and their patient interactions were billed to Medicare and Virginia Medicaid under the names of providers who had not seen the patient (sometimes doctors in another city or state), and urine drug tests were ordered at the maximum volume insurers would reimburse regardless of medical need; one doctor rented out his DEA credentials so others could prescribe Suboxone. Barnes and L5 jointly owe $4,888,426.11 restitution plus $250,000 forfeiture; co-defendants were separately ordered to pay over $1,000,000 (Dixon), over $3,000,000 (Jennifer Adams), $30,000 (Charles Wilson Adams) and $5,000 (Shaffer), and received sentences of 45, 40, 36, 24 and 18 months.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Western District of Virginia
cases.FraudEntity: Obioma Alozie Ndubuka a.k.a. 'Bank Roll' (co-conspirator/distributor); Raymono Alfonzo Russell II (co-conspirator/distributor); Dr. Rotimi Iluyomade (Annandale-based prescribing physician); Cameron Isaiah Lewis; Elhadj Malick Diallo; Zion Oluwademilade Adeduwon; Kenechukwu Brian Okwara a.k.a. 'Kene'; Yared Michael Tesfaye a.k.a. 'Yar'
cases.State_County: Virginia - Fairfax County (Annandale); Virginia - Russell County (Honaker); Virginia - Roanoke, Radford, Tazewell and Floyd; Maryland - Montgomery County and Prince George's County
cases.SchemeSummary: Co-conspirators brought Dr. Iluyomade lists of fake 'patients' (fabricated names, variations of surnames, false addresses, and identities of homeless people) and paid roughly $300 per script so he would electronically transmit fraudulent oxycodone, tussionex and promethazine-codeine prescriptions to pharmacies in numerous states; the conspirators (or paid stand-ins) picked up the filled prescriptions and resold the drugs for profit. Forfeitures total $140,000 across Russell ($40,000) and Adeduwon ($100,000).

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Oregon
cases.FraudEntity: Jahangeer Ali (owner of Oregon Clinical Laboratory); Oregon Clinical Laboratory
cases.SchemeSummary: Oregon Clinical Laboratory submitted more than $46 million in claims to Medicare Advantage plans for laboratory testing that was never ordered by any provider and never received by the listed beneficiaries; the plans paid over $28 million before Ali was arrested at LAX attempting to fly to Turkey en route to Pakistan.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of New Jersey
cases.FraudEntity: Lisa Ferraro (physician, internal medicine)
cases.SchemeSummary: Paterson internal medicine physician conspired to write oxycodone prescriptions for individuals who posed as patients, never physically examining them or asking about symptoms; she issued prescriptions for tens of thousands of 30mg oxycodone pills outside the usual course of professional practice.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Department of Justice, Criminal Division (Money Laundering, Narcotics and Forfeiture Section) and U.S. Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania
cases.FraudEntity: Bhaskar Savani (dentist, controlled Savani Group dental practices); Arun Savani (controlled finances and real property of the Savani Group); Aleksandra "Ola" Radomiak (long-term employee and executive of the Savani Group)
cases.SchemeSummary: The Savani brothers ran a racketeering enterprise ("the Savani Group") of dental practices that, after the group's Medicaid contracts were terminated, continued billing Pennsylvania Medicaid through nominee-owned dental practices and submitted claims in the names of dentists who did not treat the patients, obtaining over $32 million; proceeds were laundered through a web of companies and accounts, and the scheme also involved false H-1B visa applications, salary kickbacks from foreign workers, and obstruction of a grand jury investigation. All three defendants were convicted at trial; sentencing is pending.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of Florida
cases.FraudEntity: Douglas Craig Reid Jr. (pharmacist); Martrice Lamar Portis (conspirator)
cases.SchemeSummary: A Pensacola pharmacist and a co-conspirator were indicted for conspiring to unlawfully dispense and distribute controlled substances and to obtain controlled substances by fraud; the case is related to a prior drug-diversion prosecution charged under DOJ's 2025 National Health Care Fraud Takedown. No billing amounts or payers are identified in the document.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Michigan
cases.FraudEntity: Mohammad Hamdan (pharmacist and owner of two pharmacies)
cases.PayerName: Medicare; Medicaid; Blue Cross Blue Shield of Michigan
cases.SchemeSummary: Over a five-year period the defendant used his two pharmacies to submit false claims to Medicare, Medicaid and Blue Cross Blue Shield of Michigan for prescription drugs that were medically unnecessary or never actually dispensed; in many instances the pharmacies lacked the inventory for the drugs yet billed as if they had been dispensed, totaling over $3.2 million in claims and over $3 million in loss.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Western District of Kentucky
cases.FraudEntity: Michael Shawn Boaz (licensed pharmacist); Christopher Clayton Augustus (licensed pharmacist, co-conspirator)
cases.State_County: Kentucky - McCracken County (Paducah); Kentucky - Hickman County (Clinton)
cases.PayerName: Medicaid (Kentucky); other health care benefit programs
cases.SchemeSummary: Two pharmacists at two Kentucky pharmacies added boutique vitamins to customers' prescription orders, telling customers the vitamins were free while billing health care benefit programs $1,000-$6,000 per bottle, and submitted unauthorized prescription claims for the antihistamine Carbinoxamine Maleate purchased for $605 and billed at $2,000-$16,000 each, causing $2,185,739.52 in losses. Boaz was sentenced to 30 months and $1,806,212.90 restitution; co-conspirator Augustus pleaded guilty and awaits sentencing.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Public Affairs; U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Michigan
cases.FraudEntity: Ali Naserdean (pharmacy technician)
cases.PayerName: Medicare; Medicaid; Blue Cross Blue Shield of Michigan
cases.SchemeSummary: Working as a pharmacy technician at three metro-Detroit pharmacies, Naserdean and a co-conspirator billed Medicare, Medicaid and Blue Cross Blue Shield of Michigan over $5.6 million for prescription drugs that were never ordered by a doctor and never dispensed, using forged physician prescriptions to conceal the scheme; he also sold unlawful oxycodone prescriptions to drug traffickers for cash.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Michigan
cases.FraudEntity: Ali Naserdean (pharmacy technician)
cases.PayerName: Medicare; Medicaid; Blue Cross Blue Shield of Michigan
cases.SchemeSummary: A pharmacy technician at three metro-Detroit pharmacies and a co-conspirator billed Medicare, Medicaid and Blue Cross Blue Shield of Michigan over $5.6 million for prescription drugs that were never ordered by a doctor and never dispensed, using forged physician prescriptions to conceal the scheme; he also sold unlawful oxycodone prescriptions to drug traffickers for cash.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Pennsylvania
cases.FraudEntity: Blessings 4 Ever Home Care Agency LLC (in-home care provider); V&V Management Solutions LLC (related management services entity)
cases.SchemeSummary: Home care agency allegedly fabricated or backdated 181 training certificates and personnel documents so personal care attendants appeared to meet state and Medicaid training requirements, and billed Medicaid for their in-home services; it also billed 1,141 claims for in-home personal care for 209 beneficiaries on days those beneficiaries were hospital inpatients all day. Resolved via $1 million civil False Claims Act settlement from a qui tam action, with the relator receiving 21% of the federal recovery.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Massachusetts
cases.FraudEntity: James D. Sommers
cases.State_County: Massachusetts - Berkshire County (Pittsfield); Massachusetts - Hampshire County (Northampton)
cases.PayerName: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA); Social Security Administration
cases.SchemeSummary: Defendant allegedly stole the identity of an honorably discharged Army veteran and impersonated him for over 30 years to establish VA eligibility, obtaining nearly $30,000 in medical care and medications from VA medical centers (most recently at the Northampton, Mass. VA Medical Center in February 2026) plus thousands of dollars in Social Security benefits, and using the victim's name for transitional veterans housing.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of California
cases.FraudEntity: Felipe Ruiz (podiatrist, sole owner of West Coast Podiatry Inc.); Jose Gabriel Aguirre (pharmaceutical sales representative); West Coast Podiatry Inc.
cases.State_County: California - Fresno County; California - Madera County; California - Stanislaus County
cases.SchemeSummary: A podiatrist allowed an unlicensed pharmaceutical sales representative who sold him skin grafts to perform sharp wound debridement and apply skin grafts to Medicare/Medicaid/Medi-Cal patients unsupervised, then billed roughly $3.2 million in claims falsely representing that Ruiz or other physicians performed the procedures - including $150,000 in 2023 claims attributed to a physician who was out of the country. Forfeiture totals include nine properties plus $2.6 million (Aguirre) and $12.1 million (Ruiz) personal money judgments; both were sentenced to 63 months.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Department of Justice, Criminal Division Fraud Section and U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of Florida
cases.FraudEntity: Cory Lloyd (president of insurance brokerage firm); Steven Strong (CEO of marketing company); Dafud Iza (co-defendant)
cases.State_County: Florida - Southern District of Florida (defendant Lloyd of Stuart, Florida); Texas - Mansfield (defendant Strong)
cases.PayerName: Federal government - Affordable Care Act premium subsidies (CMS/HHS); private insurance companies paying broker commissions
cases.SchemeSummary: Lloyd and Strong used 'street marketers', sometimes paying bribes, to recruit homeless, unemployed and addicted individuals and submitted false ACA marketplace applications overstating their income so the consumers qualified for fully federally subsidized plans, generating over $233 million in claimed subsidies (at least $180 million paid) and millions in insurer commissions that Lloyd shared with Strong for referrals; they also filed thousands of Medicaid applications designed to be denied to create year-round special enrollment opportunities, and used proceeds for luxury homes, an 80-foot yacht and a Tesla. Both were sentenced to 20 years and jointly ordered to pay $180.6 million restitution; co-defendant Dafud Iza pleaded guilty and received 35 months.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of Texas
cases.FraudEntity: Osama Nahas (owner and physician, Crosspoint Medical Clinic); Isabel Pruneda (medical assistant, Crosspoint Medical Clinic)
cases.State_County: Texas - Hidalgo County (McAllen, Edinburg, Rio Grande Valley)
cases.SchemeSummary: A physician traveled to adult day care centers across the Rio Grande Valley ordering medically unnecessary lab tests and prescriptions for elderly and disabled clients, directing them to specific labs and pharmacies in exchange for kickbacks, and paid adult day care owners bribes disguised as 'rent' for facility access; his medical assistant forged patient signatures on consent forms, committed aggravated identity theft, and misappropriated pain creams distributed as 'goodie bags' to induce patients to agree to testing. Both were sentenced (120 and 97 months) and jointly ordered to pay over $3.1 million restitution to Medicare.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Missouri
cases.FraudEntity: Dr. Shazia Malik (psychiatrist employed at Behavioral Health Services LLC); Modh Azfar Malik (part-owner of Behavioral Health Services)
cases.SchemeSummary: Psychiatrist Shazia Malik billed Medicare and Missouri Medicaid for face-to-face psychotherapy she did not personally provide, including claims for dates when she was out of town and for services actually rendered by other practitioners; she settled FCA allegations for $360,000 (restitution of $155,000 to Medicare and $25,000 to Missouri Medicaid, doubled under the FCA) after pleading guilty in December 2025 to two counts of false statements relating to health care matters. Her brother and part-owner Modh Azfar Malik separately paid $501,556 in July 2025 for similar conduct.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Puerto Rico
cases.FraudEntity: Farmacia Unity (Aibonito); Raúl Morera (owner); Enid Rivera (owner); Farmacia La Rampla (Yabucoa); Edwin Gómez (owner); Farmacia Monte Verde (Bayamón); María T. Rivera (owner); Valerie Cintrón (owner); Farmacia Santa Olaya (Bayamón); Jaime Figueroa (owner)
cases.State_County: Puerto Rico - Aibonito; Puerto Rico - Yabucoa; Puerto Rico - Bayamón
cases.SchemeSummary: Four Puerto Rico pharmacies and their owners allegedly billed Medicare and Medicaid for prescription drugs that had been diverted and obtained from unverifiable sources, while misrepresenting them to patients and the programs as properly sourced from approved distributors; the four settlements total $4.6 million (with over $4.1 million collected to date), ranging from $600,000 for Farmacia Unity to $2 million for Farmacia Santa Olaya.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of New York
cases.FraudEntity: Kris Agency & Home Care, Inc. (Queens home care agency); Career Development Center of Queens, Inc. (home health aide training center)
cases.PayerName: U.S. Small Business Administration (Paycheck Protection Program)
cases.SchemeSummary: A Queens home care agency and an affiliated home health aide training center allegedly obtained over $1.8 million in second-draw PPP loans, and forgiveness of those loans, by falsely certifying that they and their affiliates had fewer than 300 employees and by failing to disclose that they were affiliates of each other; the qui tam False Claims Act case settled for $2,347,133.10 with no determination of liability.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of New York
cases.FraudEntity: Taesung Kim, a/k/a 'Terry' (pharmacy co-owner); Feng Jiang, a/k/a 'Jeff' (co-owner/co-conspirator)
cases.State_County: New York - Kings County (Brooklyn); New York - Queens County
cases.SchemeSummary: Kim co-owned retail pharmacies in Brooklyn and Queens that billed Medicare roughly $24.4 million for medically unnecessary prescription drugs obtained by paying bribes to medical providers (office rent and staff) to steer prescriptions and paying patients cash and supermarket gift certificates to fill them; proceeds were laundered through trading companies to disguise the payments and distribute profits. Kim received 63 months, $24.4M restitution and $6M forfeiture; co-conspirator Feng Jiang was previously sentenced to 15 months.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of New York; U.S. Department of Justice, National Fraud Enforcement Division
cases.FraudEntity: Taesung "Terry" Kim (co-owner of retail pharmacies); Feng "Jeff" Jiang (partner/co-conspirator)
cases.State_County: New York - Kings County (Brooklyn); New York - Queens County (Queens)
cases.SchemeSummary: Kim co-owned Brooklyn and Queens retail pharmacies that billed Medicare roughly $24.4 million for medically unnecessary prescription drugs, obtaining the prescriptions by bribing medical providers with office rent and staff and paying patients cash and supermarket gift certificates to fill them; proceeds were laundered through trading companies to disguise the kickbacks and distribute profits. Kim received 63 months, $24.4 million restitution and $6 million forfeiture; co-conspirator Feng Jiang received 15 months.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of North Carolina
cases.FraudEntity: James Shuford Price, III (owner/operator of Golden Star Labs); Golden Star Labs (Los Angeles clinical laboratory)
cases.State_County: California - Los Angeles County (Los Angeles); North Carolina - Wake County (Raleigh)
cases.PayerName: Medicaid (California Medical Assistance Program - Medi-Cal); Medicare
cases.SchemeSummary: Price's Los Angeles lab, Golden Star Labs, paid 'collectors' over $17 million on a per-specimen basis (disguised by sham fixed-fee contracts) to supply bulk bogus respiratory test samples obtained through identity theft, then billed Medi-Cal (over $85 million) and Medicare (over $11 million) for multi-panel COVID-19/flu/RSV testing using fraudulent test authorizations generated from stolen clinician identifiers, collecting more than $60 million; he also pleaded guilty to filing a false 2022 federal tax return.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of New Hampshire
cases.FraudEntity: Erik X. Alonso (psychotherapist, excluded provider); LifeWorks Counseling Associates, PLLC (telehealth mental health provider); Dr. David Ferruolo (owner)
cases.State_County: New Hampshire; Florida - Miami-Dade County (Miami, defendant's residence)
cases.SchemeSummary: Alonso, a psychotherapist on the HHS-OIG Exclusion List after a 2015 health care fraud conviction, began working in March 2022 for a New Hampshire telehealth mental health provider and caused psychotherapy/counseling sessions he rendered to be billed to New Hampshire Medicaid despite his exclusion, including claims for counseling services not provided as represented (e.g., sessions in which he asked a patient for help with personal tasks), causing roughly $173,998 in Medicaid payments; he was sentenced to a year and a day and ordered to pay $173,998.83 restitution, while the provider LifeWorks Counseling Associates and owner Dr. David Ferruolo paid $300,000 to settle parallel False Claims Act allegations.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of New York
cases.FraudEntity: Zhan Petrosyants, a/k/a 'Johnny' (organizer of no-fault clinic billing scheme; restaurateur)
cases.PayerName: New York no-fault automobile insurance companies (private auto insurers)
cases.SchemeSummary: Petrosyants and co-conspirators allegedly billed New York no-fault auto insurers tens of millions of dollars for services never rendered or medically unnecessary through nominee medical corporations that were secretly owned and controlled by non-physicians, using recruited physicians'/psychologists' license information and signatures on the claim forms. They then monetized the fraudulent receivables via advances from a law-firm-affiliated funding company, with Petrosyants taking referral fees and kickbacks (partly via blank pre-signed clinic checks), and routed advances paid to two non-medical shell corporations into a Diamond District jewelry business account.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Western District of North Carolina
cases.FraudEntity: Steven L. Mendelsohn (medical doctor, rheumatologist)
cases.SchemeSummary: The United States alleged that in 2019 the rheumatologist purchased intravenous immunosuppressive arthritis drugs that were intended for foreign markets and not obtained from a licensed or authorized U.S. distributor, administered them to patients, and then sought full Medicare reimbursement for these FDA-unapproved drugs; he agreed to pay $549,554.26 to resolve the False Claims Act allegations.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Rhode Island
cases.FraudEntity: Nadine Jean Baptiste (Rhode Island Department of Human Services supervisor)
cases.State_County: Rhode Island - Kent County (Warwick); Rhode Island - Providence County (Providence)
cases.SchemeSummary: A RI Department of Human Services supervisor used her official access to repeatedly obtain SNAP EBT card information, make unauthorized telephonic balance inquiries and change card PINs - often for juvenile, homeless or incarcerated recipients - and, with her daughter, allegedly used the diverted benefits for personal purchases; EBT cards holding more than $300,000 in benefits were improperly accessed.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Western District of New York
cases.FraudEntity: John Weinmann (independent insurance broker)
cases.SchemeSummary: Weinmann, an independent insurance broker, agreed with a Syracuse, NY company to target Low Income Subsidy Medicare beneficiaries and was paid a kickback for each prescription medication he got filled and paid for under a beneficiary's Medicare coverage; he recommended and arranged purchases of medically unnecessary prescription drugs, receiving $32,150 in kickbacks. Sentenced to three years' probation and a $2,000 fine.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Louisiana
cases.FraudEntity: Daniel Iulian Teutoc, a/k/a 'Simon Mikula'; Constantin Calin (codefendant)
cases.State_County: Louisiana - St. John the Baptist Parish (Laplace); St. Tammany Parish (Slidell); Jefferson Parish (Harvey); St. Charles Parish (Boutte); St. Bernard Parish (Chalmette); Orleans Parish (New Orleans)
cases.SchemeSummary: Defendant and a codefendant visited Walmart stores across southeast Louisiana and used magnets to activate card-skimming devices previously installed at points of sale by other conspirators, downloading stolen credit, debit and EBT card data to their cell phones and forwarding it to a coconspirator so fraudulent charges could be made; not a health care payer fraud, though restitution of over $11 million was agreed.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Department of Justice, Criminal Division, Fraud Section; U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of Texas
cases.FraudEntity: Nikolai Buzolin (registered owner/president of Verisola, Inc.); Verisola, Inc. (durable medical equipment company)
cases.PayerName: Medicare (Medicare Advantage Organizations administering Medicare Part C)
cases.SchemeSummary: Buzolin registered Verisola, Inc. as a DME supplier in Houston and opened eight bank accounts at eight institutions using false documentation claiming sole ownership; Verisola then submitted over $400 million in claims to Medicare Advantage Organizations for orthotic braces and glucose monitors never provided, collecting at least $1.7 million, of which at least $1.2 million was wired to overseas entities and accounts.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of California
cases.FraudEntity: Circle Medical Care of California; Circle Medical Technologies, Inc.; Dr. Nicole Tsang, D.O. (Chief Medical Officer and medical director)
cases.PayerName: Medicare; Medicaid (California); TRICARE; California commercial insurers
cases.SchemeSummary: Circle's telehealth platform submitted claims to Medicare, Medicaid, TRICARE and California commercial insurers listing the name and NPI of rendering providers who did not actually perform or supervise the services, and failed to properly supervise the nurse practitioners and physician assistants who treated patients; resolved via a $3,325,000 False Claims Act settlement ($475,000 federal, $2,850,000 California) arising from a qui tam action.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Middle District of Florida
cases.FraudEntity: Allin IP DX LLC (laboratory)
cases.SchemeSummary: Allin IP DX, a Sarasota lab, paid remuneration to independent marketers in exchange for referrals of lab specimens from Medicare beneficiaries, resulting in false claims to Medicare; the lab self-disclosed and settled for $980,000.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of New York
cases.SchemeSummary: No specific fraud case is described. The press release announces the revival of the NDNY Health Care Fraud Task Force, convening federal agencies (FBI, HHS-OIG, DCIS, DEA, VA-OIG), New York State agencies (MFCU, OMIG, OSC, DFS, BNE), a program integrity contractor, and private insurers (UnitedHealthcare, MVP, Excellus BCBS, Fidelis, CDPHP, MetLife) to coordinate health care fraud investigations and enforcement.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Pennsylvania
cases.FraudEntity: Dr. Bhaskar Savani (dentist, co-owner of the Savani Group); Arun Savani (co-owner, controlled Savani Group finances); Aleksandra Radomiak a/k/a 'Ola' (associate); Savani Group
cases.State_County: Pennsylvania - Philadelphia; Pennsylvania - Montgomery County (Ambler, Blue Bell, Lansdale)
cases.SchemeSummary: After Savani Group dental practices were terminated from Medicaid contracts, the brothers used nominee business owners to re-obtain Medicaid contracts and bill Medicaid, defrauding the program of more than $30 million; they also submitted false Medicaid bills under another dentist's NPI on dates when that dentist was outside the United States and for services actually performed by uncredentialed dentists, then laundered the proceeds through a web of corporate bank accounts. The enterprise also involved H-1B visa fraud with wage kickbacks from foreign workers, tax/wire fraud on roughly $1.6 million of unreported personal income and $1.1 million of employee income, and implanting FDA-uncleared prototype dental implants labeled 'Not For Human Use' in patients. Figures span three convicted defendants tried together.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of Texas
cases.FraudEntity: Tronown Thomas (licensed pharmacist, owner/operator of Rayford ACP Pharmacy); Rayford ACP Pharmacy
cases.PayerName: Department of Labor Office of Workers' Compensation Programs (DOL-OWCP)
cases.SchemeSummary: Thomas, a pharmacist who owned Rayford ACP Pharmacy, paid over $2 million in kickbacks to a Houston clinic owner in exchange for referrals of DOL-OWCP-insured patients prescribed high-reimbursement compounded medications, then billed DOL-OWCP for those compounded drugs, receiving more than $20 million in reimbursements.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Middle District of Pennsylvania
cases.FraudEntity: Scranton Heart Institute (cardiology practice)
cases.SchemeSummary: SHI allegedly accepted remuneration from a mobile PET scan company - substantial hourly payments labeled as professional supervision fees plus the ability to bill and keep the Medicare professional component for the mobile imaging - to induce referral of its Medicare patients for PET scans, making the resulting claims false under the Anti-Kickback Statute and the physician self-referral (Stark) law.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of Texas
cases.FraudEntity: Emylee Thai (owner/operator of genetic testing laboratory); David Jenson (podiatrist); Nestor Rafael Romero Magallanes (self-proclaimed CEO of a local medical clinic)
cases.State_County: Texas - Southern District of Texas (Houston); Texas - Spring
cases.SchemeSummary: Annual district collections release describing two health care fraud matters: Emylee Thai allegedly owned a lab that billed Medicare for medically unnecessary genetic testing induced by kickbacks, with false dates of service and diagnosis codes to inflate reimbursement (she fled the country; a civil forfeiture default judgment forfeited about $5 million in real property), and David Jenson and Nestor Rafael Romero Magallanes allegedly billed Medicare about $90 million for skin substitute products for patients with no qualifying wounds, falsifying medical records to support the claims, with roughly $83 million in alleged proceeds (nearly $70 million in cryptocurrency) seized and subject to pending forfeiture.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of New Jersey
cases.FraudEntity: SEA BOX, Inc. (shipping container designer/manufacturer, government contractor)
FraudTypeAll: Government procurement contract violation (False Claims Act)
cases.SchemeSummary: Under approximately 35 Defense Logistics Agency contracts to supply ISO shipping containers to the Army and Air Force, Sea Box shipped the containers on cheaper foreign-flagged vessels in violation of the Cargo Preference Act and contract terms, lowering its bid costs and undercutting compliant competitors, then gave military authorities inaccurate and misleading information when questioned; it agreed to pay $2.6 million plus interest over three years under the civil False Claims Act. Not a health care payer case.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of Indiana
cases.FraudEntity: Don J. Wagoner (former physician, sole owner); Wagoner Medical Center, L.L.C.
cases.SchemeSummary: Patients seeking opioid prescriptions were required to give a single urine sample, which was tested once with a roughly $10 multiplexed screening kit covering nine or more drug classes; defendants then billed Indiana Medicaid $171.27 or more per patient by falsely certifying that nine or more separate samples had been collected and analyzed, instead of the allowed $20.83, across over 5,000 claims for nearly $1 million in overpayments, resolved by a False Claims Act settlement of nearly $1.7 million.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Virginia
cases.FraudEntity: Lori Ann Talens (creator/seller of counterfeit coupons); Pacifico Talens Jr. (husband, assisted and profited); Sherise Williams (bulk purchaser); Amber Lynn Teague, aka Amber Johnson (purchaser); Jennifer Irene Snyder (purchaser); Melissa Kay Apodaca (purchaser); Cindi Suzette Swindle (purchaser)
cases.SchemeSummary: Lori Ann Talens designed and printed counterfeit manufacturer coupons, often with inflated values, at her Virginia Beach home and sold them in bulk via social media and apps to coupon enthusiasts (customers received about $50 in counterfeit coupons per $1 paid), causing roughly $31.8 million in losses to retailers and manufacturers; her husband assisted and profited. Seven defendants were sentenced (longest 12 years for Lori Ann Talens; Williams' purchases alone caused an estimated $991,067 loss), and Lori Ann Talens also pleaded guilty to wire fraud and health care fraud for a separate, unspecified scheme.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Michigan
cases.FraudEntity: Samer Kammo; Rita Shaba (co-defendant); Christina Anasi (Kammo's wife, awaiting sentencing)
cases.SchemeSummary: Kammo and co-conspirators submitted fraudulent Paycheck Protection Program loan applications for several business entities, misrepresenting payroll information, falsely certifying permissible use of funds, and supporting the applications with fictitious payroll, health insurance, bank and tax records; they also misused personal identifying information of Kammo's family members. Kammo and family received nearly $2.5 million in PPP funds; he received 36 months and $2,493,348.50 restitution, while co-defendant Rita Shaba received 27 months.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of New Jersey
cases.FraudEntity: Sherif Elmasri (pharmacy owner/pharmacist); Boris Veysman (emergency medicine doctor); Stephanie Cupo (employee of Veysman, prior authorizations); Nikki Steidle (advanced practice nurse); Janet Tadros (office manager of neurology practice); Ashlee Maixner (advanced practice nurse)
cases.State_County: New Jersey - Monmouth County (Morganville, Freehold); New Jersey - Middlesex County (South Plainfield); New Jersey - Ocean County (Toms River, Lakehurst); New Jersey - Hudson County (Union City, Jersey City)
cases.SchemeSummary: Pharmacy owner Elmasri paid cash kickbacks to a doctor, nurse practitioners and a neurology office manager to issue medically unnecessary prescriptions for high-reimbursement medications he selected, which his pharmacies then billed to Medicare and Medicaid; some prescriptions were issued without examining patients or without the prescriber's knowledge, and an employee submitted prior authorizations containing false information to get them approved. Five of the six defendants pleaded guilty; Maixner was indicted and pleaded not guilty.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Western District of Virginia
cases.FraudEntity: Carolyn Bryant-Taylor (owner, 1st Adult N Pediatric Healthcare Services); Kafomdi Josephine Okocha (owner); Samuel Okocha (owner); Shekita Gore (director of nursing); Eno Utuk (nurse/personal care employee); Elizabeth Ilome (nurse/personal care employee); 1st Adult N Pediatric Healthcare Services (home health agency)
cases.SchemeSummary: Owners and staff of a Medicaid-enrolled home health agency billed Virginia Medicaid for private duty nursing, personal care and respite services that were never provided or were billed in excess of services actually rendered, supporting the claims with falsified records; two owners paid parents/guardians of patients for blank, pre-signed nursing notes that were then filled out to justify billing. Six defendants sentenced (longest 120 months) with $10 million total restitution ordered.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Louisiana
cases.FraudEntity: John Dennis Michael Peyroux (chiropractor, clinic owner); Steven D. Peyroux (brother, co-conspirator)
cases.SchemeSummary: Peyroux bought Medicare beneficiary identifiers and fabricated audio recordings of people posing as beneficiaries 'requesting' over-the-counter COVID-19 test kits, then billed Medicare through his chiropractic clinic for kits that were never requested, including for beneficiaries who were deceased or in hospice/inpatient care and thus ineligible; he also misappropriated a former nurse practitioner's credentials to list her falsely as the referring provider. He billed about $3.3 million in roughly six months and was reimbursed about $3.2 million; restitution of $3,212,761.44 was ordered plus over $1 million forfeited from his bank accounts. His brother Steven D. Peyroux pleaded guilty and awaits sentencing.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Louisiana
cases.FraudEntity: Robert Tassin, M.D. (physician working for purported telemedicine companies)
cases.State_County: Louisiana - Slidell (St. Tammany Parish); New Orleans
cases.SchemeSummary: Working for purported telemedicine companies, Tassin signed doctors' orders for cancer genetic (CGx) tests for Medicare beneficiaries he never saw, spoke to, or treated, falsely certifying in medical records that the tests were medically necessary; he was paid a set fee (typically $30) per order, and the orders generated over $6.6 million in claims to Medicare, of which over $2 million was paid. Sentenced to three years probation (first 12 months home confinement), $2,043,542.23 restitution and $106,757 forfeiture.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Department of Justice, Civil Division and U.S. Attorney's Office, District of South Carolina
cases.FraudEntity: LTD Holding LLC, formerly known as Labtech Diagnostics LLC (clinical laboratory); Joseph Labash (founder and CEO)
cases.State_County: South Carolina - Anderson County (Anderson); North Carolina - Mecklenburg County (Charlotte); North Carolina - Rowan County (Landis)
cases.SchemeSummary: Labtech and its CEO allegedly paid doctors five types of kickbacks - disguised as office space rent, phlebotomy and toxicology payments, an inflated purchase price for used lab equipment from a Charlotte physician practice, and free drug-screen services/supplies to a Landis pain practice - to induce referrals of laboratory testing billed to federal health care programs, concealing the payments via hand-delivered money orders, sham contracts, and falsified square footage and hours on 'fraud and abuse' certification forms. Labtech pleaded guilty to five Anti-Kickback counts and will pay $103,551.90 restitution, while Labtech and Labash jointly agreed to a $6.8 million civil FCA settlement (plus up to $3,271,536 more contingently); total DOJ recoveries relating to Labtech, including nine doctors, exceed $11.5 million, with the relator receiving $1.36 million.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Kentucky
cases.FraudEntity: John Quintrell (sole owner of Civil LLC); Civil LLC (mining business)
cases.SchemeSummary: Quintrell, sole owner of coal mining company Civil LLC, withheld federal income and FICA (Medicare/Social Security) taxes from employee paychecks but willfully failed to account for and pay over approximately $22.1 million, including the employer's share of payroll taxes, to the IRS; no health care payer was billed.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Delaware
cases.FraudEntity: Ty Mauldin (medical biller and credentialer)
FraudTypeAll: Identity theft to divert controlled substances
cases.SchemeSummary: Mauldin used his job access as a medical biller/credentialer to steal medical professionals' licensure information and order thousands of opioid pills for himself from wholesale pharmaceutical suppliers; he also falsified his own electronic medical records to pose as a cancer patient and obtain pain management services (intrathecal pain pump, opioid prescriptions) paid by his private insurer, and falsely held himself out as a licensed nurse to perform Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation therapy on patients that was then billed to Medicaid.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of Texas
cases.FraudEntity: Javier Cabello (doctor/owner); Ammar Halloum (doctor/owner); Jamil Madi (doctor/owner); Jairo Rodriguez (doctor/owner); Ricardo Schwarcz (doctor/owner); Stanley Sy (doctor/owner); Benchmark Inpatient Services PLLC dba Beyond Inpatient Services; Brownsville Pulmonary Center, P.A. dba Benchmark Pulmonary Center
cases.State_County: Texas - Cameron County (Harlingen, Brownsville, San Benito, Olmito, Rancho Viejo); Texas - Hidalgo County (Weslaco, Pharr)
cases.SchemeSummary: Six doctors and their inpatient and pulmonary practices allegedly billed Medicare, Medicaid and TRICARE for critical care services on stable patients, unnecessary follow-up visits, or visits never performed, and billed routine or never-performed pulmonary function testing not supported by medical records; the group collectively agreed to pay $4,855,844 to resolve the qui tam False Claims Act allegations.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of Iowa
cases.FraudEntity: Eugene J. Cherny (plastic surgeon); Heartland Plastic & Reconstructive Surgery, P.C.; Genesis Health System; Mercy Health Network, Inc.; Trinity Health Corporation
cases.State_County: Iowa - Polk County (Des Moines); Iowa - Scott County (Davenport)
cases.SchemeSummary: Two Southern District of Iowa matters announced in the 2026 national takedown: (1) a civil False Claims Act complaint alleging Dr. Eugene Cherny and his practice obtained dual invoices from a skin-substitute distributor and submitted only the artificially inflated 'list price' invoice to a Medicare contractor, resulting in more than $2 million in federal health program payments; and (2) a $4,643,128 settlement, following voluntary self-disclosure, with Genesis Health System, Mercy Health Network and Trinity Health over Genesis's overuse and consequent over-billing of the Impella heart pump device from April 2016 to March 2022.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Missouri
cases.FraudEntity: Daniell Green (owner/operator of A&L Angels Home Healthcare Services LLC); Dejuan Bingham; Kimberly Diazascencio; Thomas Keith; A&L Angels Home Healthcare Services LLC
cases.SchemeSummary: Indictment alleges the owner of a Bridgeton home health company and her associates billed Missouri Medicaid $1.46 million using fabricated timesheets for home health services never rendered - including on dates patients were hospitalized or when listed workers were working elsewhere - and recruited Medicaid patients to lend their names to false claims; the owner also allegedly submitted a false participation agreement claiming providers were on the Family Care Safety Registry and background-checked, concealing a co-defendant's felony conviction, with proceeds spent on vacations and luxury goods.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of New York
cases.FraudEntity: Center for Disability Services Holding Corporation, d/b/a St. Margaret's Center (skilled nursing facility)
cases.SchemeSummary: A skilled nursing facility caring for medically fragile children billed federal and state Medicaid for care alleged to be grossly substandard and therefore worthless (insufficient nursing staff, medication errors, deficient respiratory/tracheostomy care), and annually falsely certified as a condition of payment that it had adopted and implemented an effective quality-of-care compliance program; resolved for $1.3 million plus a five-year HHS-OIG Corporate Integrity Agreement following a qui tam suit by two former employees who receive about $247,000.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Massachusetts
