cases.FraudEntity: Stern Therapy Consultants (long-term care therapy provider); RegalCare Management Group, LLC and RegalCare Management 2.0 (skilled nursing facility operator, case ongoing); Eliyahu Mirlis (RegalCare owner, case ongoing); Hector Caraballo (RegalCare executive, case ongoing)
cases.SchemeSummary: Stern's therapists delivered Ultra High RUG skilled nursing facility rehabilitation therapy - the highest-reimbursing tier - to RegalCare's Medicare patients after documenting that therapy should stop and after patients said they were unable or refused to perform it, causing RegalCare to bill Medicare for medically unnecessary services; a Stern Senior Regional Director with no clinical license also certified that a terminated employee had performed Ultra High RUG therapy for a patient without confirming the services occurred, to justify billing. Stern paid $315,000 (relator share $61,875) to settle; claims against RegalCare, Mirlis and Caraballo remain pending.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of Illinois
cases.FraudEntity: Seung Han Lim (chiropractor, owner of Movement Health and Rehab, aka Motu Chiropractic and Motu Chiromassage); Movement Health and Rehab
cases.PayerName: Blue Cross Blue Shield of Illinois
cases.SchemeSummary: Chiropractor billed Blue Cross Blue Shield of Illinois more than $600,000 for chiropractic services never rendered, including claims for dates when he or the patient were out of state and claims for services purportedly provided by another chiropractor to Lim and his own family; when the insurer audited, he created and submitted false patient medical records to support the bogus claims.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Massachusetts
cases.FraudEntity: John Doe (suspected Dominican national, unlawfully residing in Boston; true identity unknown)
cases.SchemeSummary: Defendant allegedly used a U.S. citizen's stolen identity and Social Security number, falsely representing himself as a U.S. citizen in a MassHealth healthcare benefits application and supporting sworn affidavit, thereby obtaining over $30,000 in MassHealth (Massachusetts Medicaid) benefits for which he was ineligible; he was also charged with possession with intent to distribute a fentanyl analogue and aggravated identity theft.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Western District of New York
cases.FraudEntity: Timothy Klein (operator of JRS Group, LLC); JRS Group, LLC
cases.PayerName: Medicare; Medicare Part D drug plan sponsors; Medicaid
cases.SchemeSummary: Klein, through JRS Group, paid kickbacks to insurance brokers who recruited Medicare beneficiaries for 'no cost' prescription drugs, paid Advanced Telehealth for doctors to conduct telemedicine visits and sign prescriptions Klein had preselected/pre-filled, then collected per-prescription payments from ProRX and SunRise Pharmacy (e.g., a $95,479.05 check from ProRx on Sept. 17, 2018) for medically unnecessary drugs billed to Medicare Part D.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Department of Justice, Civil Division and U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of California
cases.FraudEntity: Takeda Pharmaceuticals, U.S.A. Inc. (drug manufacturer)
cases.PayerName: Medicare; TRICARE; other federal health care programs
cases.SchemeSummary: Takeda allegedly paid healthcare providers speaker-bureau honoraria and high-end restaurant meals - including for duplicate programs on the same topic with no educational benefit - to induce them to prescribe the antidepressant Trintellix, causing false claims for those prescriptions to be submitted to Medicare and other federal health care programs; resolved for $13,670,921.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of California
cases.FraudEntity: Takeda Pharmaceuticals, U.S.A., Inc. (pharmaceutical manufacturer)
cases.PayerName: Medicare; other federal health care programs
cases.SchemeSummary: Takeda allegedly paid healthcare providers speaker-bureau honoraria and high-end restaurant meals to induce them to prescribe the antidepressant Trintellix, including paying prescribers to attend duplicative speaker programs with no educational value, thereby causing false claims for the drug to be submitted to Medicare and other federal health care programs.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Michigan
cases.FraudEntity: Team Rehabilitation Services, LLC ("Team Rehab") (operator of approximately 140 physical therapy clinics)
cases.PayerName: Medicare; Medicaid; TRICARE; Federal Employees Health Benefits Program (FEHBP); U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs
cases.SchemeSummary: Team Rehab billed federal health care programs using time-based CPT codes reserved for one-to-one physical therapy, when the therapy was actually delivered in a group setting without sufficient direct one-on-one patient contact, thereby collecting higher payment than warranted. Resolved for $4,969,494 following a qui tam suit; the whistleblower receives $919,356.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Department of Justice, Criminal Division, Fraud Section (Office of Public Affairs)
cases.FraudEntity: Christopher Harwood (owner/operator of telemedicine company TelevisitMD and multiple Florida DME supply companies)
cases.SchemeSummary: Harwood used telemarketing to recruit Medicare beneficiaries for unnecessary orthotic braces and genetic tests, paid doctors through his telemedicine company TelevisitMD to sign orders without legitimate patient relationships or compliant telehealth visits, then sold the signed orders to DME suppliers, labs and marketers and also billed Medicare through his own Florida DME companies; $46.2 million in false claims were submitted, Medicare paid $17.9 million and Harwood personally received over $10.4 million.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Department of Justice, Criminal Division, Fraud Section
cases.FraudEntity: Reinaldo Wilson (owner of two telemedicine companies)
cases.SchemeSummary: Wilson used two New Jersey telemedicine companies to pay kickbacks to medical providers to sign orders for medically unnecessary orthotic braces for Medicare beneficiaries, then sold the signed orders to marketing companies that resold them to DME brace suppliers, which billed Medicare over $56 million (Medicare paid $27.9 million); he also set up a new telemedicine company in a church member's name using $20,000 from her to conceal the scheme.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Department of Justice, Criminal Division, Fraud Section; Southern District of Texas
cases.FraudEntity: James Robles (medical doctor, owner/operator of cash-only Houston clinic)
cases.SchemeSummary: Robles allegedly ran a cash-only Houston clinic selling prescriptions for oxycodone, hydrocodone and carisoprodol to 'crew leaders' who recruited people to pose as patients; he often prescribed without seeing or examining them, and the pills (approx. 2.9M hydrocodone, 1.3M oxycodone, 1.1M carisoprodol over four years) were filled at complicit pharmacies and resold on the black market, with more than $2 million in cash deposited into his accounts.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Department of Justice, Criminal Division, Fraud Section; U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas
cases.FraudEntity: Michael Taba (orthopedic surgeon); co-defendant pharmacy owners (owners/operators of three pharmacies in Fort Worth and Arlington, Texas)
cases.State_County: Texas - Tarrant County (Fort Worth, Arlington); Texas - Collin County (McKinney)
cases.PayerName: U.S. Department of Labor Office of Workers' Compensation Programs (DOL-OWCP); Blue Cross Blue Shield
cases.SchemeSummary: Pharmacy owners paid Dr. Taba and other doctors millions in bribes to write prescriptions for medically unnecessary compound creams for injured federal workers; the creams were mixed by untrained teenagers in pharmacy back rooms at about $15 per prescription and billed to DOL-OWCP and Blue Cross Blue Shield for as much as $16,000 each, totaling over $145 million billed and more than $90 million paid. Taba was convicted at trial and sentenced to 102 months with over $13 million restitution.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Department of Justice, Criminal Division, Fraud Section (Health Care Fraud Strike Force)
cases.FraudEntity: Robert "Bobby" Leon Smith III (owner/operator of seven durable medical equipment supply companies and a marketing company)
cases.State_County: Texas - Archer City (Archer County); Florida; Maryland
cases.SchemeSummary: Smith used a Texas marketing company and an offshore call center in the Philippines to pressure Medicare beneficiaries nationwide into accepting medically unnecessary orthotic braces, foot baths, and genetic tests; he paid kickbacks to illegitimate telemedicine companies for doctors' orders (later using forged physician signatures), billed Medicare through his seven DME companies, and sold surplus orders to other suppliers who he knew would submit false claims, totaling $61.5 million.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of Georgia
cases.FraudEntity: Access DX Laboratory (Houston, Texas laboratory); Michael Stewart (former CEO); Harold Shatz (Florida businessman)
cases.SchemeSummary: Access DX, a Houston lab, together with its CEO and a Florida businessman, allegedly paid kickbacks to marketers for referrals of Medicare and Medicaid beneficiaries for genetic testing, paid telemedicine providers for false doctors' orders, unbundled genetic testing billing codes, and billed for medically unnecessary genetic tests; the $36.4 million civil FCA settlement is combined across the lab and the two individuals, who also pleaded guilty criminally in the Southern District of Texas, and includes a $7.2 million whistleblower share.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Department of Justice, Civil Division, Commercial Litigation Branch, Fraud Section; U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of Georgia
cases.FraudEntity: Access DX Laboratory (Houston, Texas clinical laboratory); Michael Stewart (former CEO of Access DX); Harold Shatz (Florida businessman)
cases.SchemeSummary: Access DX, its former CEO and a Florida businessman allegedly paid kickbacks to marketers for referrals of Medicare/Medicaid beneficiaries for genetic testing, paid telemedicine providers to generate false doctors' orders for medically unnecessary tests, and unbundled genetic testing billing codes to increase reimbursement; the three defendants together paid $36.4 million to resolve FCA claims (whistleblower receiving $7.2 million), with both individuals also agreeing to plead guilty to conspiracy under 18 U.S.C. § 371.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of New Hampshire (with the New England Strike Force)
cases.FraudEntity: Kakha Bendeliani (alleged associate of Transnational Criminal Organization, money laundering); Goga Danelia (alleged associate of Transnational Criminal Organization, money laundering); Centennial Med Supply LLC (fraudulent DME company linked to the defendants)
cases.State_County: New Hampshire; New England and nationwide
cases.PayerName: Medicare; Medicare Supplemental Insurers; private health insurance companies
cases.SchemeSummary: A Russia-based transnational criminal organization allegedly used stolen identities of Medicare beneficiaries and doctors to submit nearly $3 billion in claims for durable medical equipment (e.g., catheters) that was never prescribed or delivered, with Medicare and supplemental insurers paying at least about $12.5 million to Centennial Med Supply LLC. Bendeliani and Danelia are charged with conspiring to launder the proceeds by using nominee owners with false sale and corporate registration documents to open bank accounts, then funneling the fraud payments through shell companies to overseas banks.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Department of Justice, National Fraud Enforcement Division (Office of Public Affairs)
cases.FraudEntity: Unnamed defendants in multiple cases, including two men convicted in a genetic testing scheme; a former NFL player; an optometric physician (Tennessee practice owner); a pharmacy technician (Michigan); a behavioral health biller (Oklahoma City); tax preparers (Florida and California); four defendants including two former U.S. Postal Service employees
cases.State_County: Pennsylvania (Middle District); Florida (South Florida; Jacksonville); Michigan; Tennessee; Oklahoma - Oklahoma City; California; New York
cases.PayerName: Medicare; Medicaid; private health insurance companies; Civilian Health and Medical Program of the Department of Veterans Affairs (CHAMPVA); U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs; workers' compensation insurers
cases.SchemeSummary: Roundup press release summarizing multiple unrelated enforcement actions totaling nearly $1 billion. Health care items include over $522 million in claims to Medicare, Medicaid and private insurers for medically unnecessary genetic tests (151- and 36-month sentences); a nearly $200 million Medicare/CHAMPVA conspiracy by a former NFL player (over 16 years in prison, $110 million restitution and about $17 million forfeiture); a Tennessee optometric physician billing Medicare $6.9 million for wound care products never purchased or used; a Michigan pharmacy technician billing Medicare/Medicaid $5.6 million for prescriptions never dispensed while selling oxycodone prescriptions for cash; and an Oklahoma City defendant sentenced to 20 months for $1.1 million in false private-insurance claims for behavioral health counseling sessions purportedly given to family members. Figures span multiple defendants and separate cases.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Department of Justice, National Fraud Enforcement Division (Health Care Fraud Section), with the U.S. Attorney's Offices for the District of Arizona, District of Nevada, and Northern District of California
cases.FraudEntity: Gehrke and King (wound graft company owners, D. Ariz.); Ali (owner of a Pakistan-based medical billing company, D. Ariz.); Schena (president of a Silicon Valley medical technology company, N.D. Cal.); unnamed CEO and Chief Medical Officer of a digital health technology company (N.D. Cal.)
cases.State_County: Arizona; Nevada; California - Northern District (San Francisco)
cases.PayerName: Medicare; Medicaid (Arizona Medicaid); TRICARE; private insurers
cases.SchemeSummary: Announcement of the launch of the West Coast Health Care Fraud Strike Force rather than a single prosecution; it recaps prior matters spanning multiple defendants: a $1.2 billion wound graft billing scheme against Medicare and Medicaid (Gehrke and King, sentenced to 15.5 and 14 years, $126 million in cash, luxury vehicles and gold bars seized), an indicted Pakistan-based biller alleged to have exploited substance abuse patients at over 41 clinics to bill Arizona Medicaid more than $650 million, Schena's COVID-19 testing securities/kickback case (8-year sentence), and a digital health company CEO/CMO convicted of a $100 million scheme tied to internet Adderall prescribing.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Middle District of Pennsylvania
cases.SchemeSummary: Not a fraud case: this press release announces the Senate confirmation of Brian D. Miller as United States Attorney for the Middle District of Pennsylvania and summarizes his career, which included service as Special Counsel on Health Care Fraud. No fraud scheme, defendant, or loss amount is described.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Department of Justice, National Fraud Enforcement Division (Office of Public Affairs); seizure authorized by federal court in Los Angeles
cases.FraudEntity: Unnamed Michigan pharmacy technician; Expert Wound Care PC (California-based clinic)
cases.SchemeSummary: Figures span two separate health care matters in a DOJ weekly roundup: a Michigan pharmacy technician pleaded guilty to a $5.6 million scheme billing Medicare, Medicaid and private insurers for prescription drugs he never dispensed and to illegally supplying oxycodone prescriptions to drug traffickers for cash; and Expert Wound Care PC, a California clinic, submitted over $46.6 million in Medicare claims (about $34 million paid) for skin graft substitutes and services never provided, leading to a court-authorized seizure of roughly $2 million.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Department of Justice, National Fraud Enforcement Division (with U.S. Attorney Daniel Rosen, Minnesota)
cases.FraudEntity: 15 unnamed defendants charged in Minnesota Medicaid fraud schemes
cases.SchemeSummary: DOJ announced charges against 15 defendants who allegedly participated in various schemes to defraud federal benefit programs, principally Medicaid, totaling over $90 million in intended loss, including what the Department described as the two largest Medicaid fraud cases ever charged in Minnesota and first-of-their-kind charges involving certain Medicaid programs; the document does not describe the billing mechanics.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Department of Justice — Civil Division; U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of Illinois
cases.FraudEntity: Symphony Jackson Square LLC d/b/a Symphony of Chicago West (skilled nursing facility); Symphony Park South LLC d/b/a Symphony of Morgan Park (skilled nursing facility); Symphony Midway LLC (skilled nursing facility)
cases.SchemeSummary: Three affiliated Illinois skilled nursing facilities allegedly billed Medicare for physical, occupational and speech therapy provided for longer than medically necessary and without regard to individual patient needs, inflating patients' resource utilization group (RUG) levels to obtain higher per-week reimbursement; they agreed to pay $300,000 (ability-to-pay based), with $45,000 to the qui tam relator Integra Med Analytics LLC.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Columbia; Superior Court of the District of Columbia
cases.FraudEntity: Nelson Kuma (psychiatric counselor, Psychiatric Institute of Washington); Richard Hounnou (psychiatric counselor, Psychiatric Institute of Washington); Norma Munoz-Bent (registered nurse, Psychiatric Institute of Washington)
cases.SchemeSummary: Not a billing scheme: three Psychiatric Institute of Washington staff members (two psychiatric counselors and a registered nurse) allegedly found a 58-year-old patient unresponsive and not breathing but failed to assess him, perform CPR, or provide any lifesaving measures for at least 21 minutes, after which he could not be resuscitated; the case was investigated by the D.C. OIG Medicaid Fraud Control Unit and charged as criminal negligence.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of New York
cases.FraudEntity: Anthony Santamaria (managed teams of billers); Hershel Tsikman (coordinated laundering of proceeds through straw owners and shell entities); Hafizullah Ebady (coordinated pharmacy purchases, on-the-ground manager); Dela Saidazim (recruited physicians, personal assistant); David Bishoff (pharmacy logistics); Brycen Millett (oversaw call centers); Joshua Alegria (custom software, forwarded fraudulent prescriptions); Brian Sutton (leader, at large)
cases.State_County: New York - Kings County (Brooklyn); New York - Richmond County (Staten Island); New York - New York County (Manhattan); New York - Long Island; New Jersey; Pennsylvania; Texas; Michigan; Alabama; Utah
cases.SchemeSummary: Moscow-based organization used call centers in Utah and Russia to cold-call privately insured beneficiaries offering no-cost medications without exams, then generated fraudulent prescriptions under recruited physicians' names and NPI numbers though in most cases no telemedicine visit occurred and many beneficiaries never received medications; the group bought dozens of brick-and-mortar pharmacies through straw owners and had Moscow-based billers remotely submit over $1.97 billion in claims, of which private insurers paid over $758 million, with proceeds laundered through shell companies. Figures span all eight co-defendants; forfeiture totals $3.2 million (Santamaria) and over $1.8 million (Ebady), with restitution to be determined.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of New York; U.S. Department of Justice, Criminal Division / National Fraud Enforcement Division; U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of New York
cases.FraudEntity: Anthony Santamaria (trained and managed teams of billers submitting reimbursement requests); Hershel Tsikman (coordinated laundering of proceeds through straw owners and shell entities); Hafizullah Ebady (coordinated pharmacy purchases, 'boots-on-the-ground manager' for at least 30 pharmacies); Dela Saidazim (recruited licensed physicians, personal assistant to leader); David Bishoff (coordinated pharmacy logistics); Brycen Millett (oversaw call centers in Utah and Russia); Joshua Alegria (oversaw custom software, forwarded fraudulent prescriptions to physicians); Brian Sutton (leader of the Moscow-based criminal organization, at large)
cases.State_County: New York - Kings County (Brooklyn); New York - Richmond County (Staten Island); New York - New York County (Manhattan); New York - Long Island; New Jersey; Pennsylvania; Texas; Michigan; Alabama; Utah (call centers); Moscow, Russia (operations)
cases.SchemeSummary: A Moscow-based organization ran call centers (first in Utah, later Russia) that cold-called privately insured beneficiaries offering free medications without exams, then generated prescriptions under recruited physicians' names and NPI numbers even though the purported telemedicine visits never occurred and many beneficiaries never received the drugs; the group bought dozens of brick-and-mortar pharmacies nationwide through straw owners and used Moscow-based 'billers' to remotely submit over $1.97 billion in claims, of which private insurers paid over $758 million, with proceeds laundered through pass-through shell companies. Figures and sentences span multiple co-defendants: Santamaria and Tsikman each 120 months, Ebady 97 months, Saidazim time served; forfeitures of $3.2 million (Santamaria) and over $1.8 million (Ebady), restitution to be determined.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Department of Justice, Criminal Division Fraud Section; U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of Florida
cases.FraudEntity: Marco Scamarone (owner/operator of DME companies); Jose Mendez (owner/operator of DME companies); Renee Vazquez (owner/operator of DME companies); Braces and Orthotics LLC (DME company); Stone Oak Durable Medical Equipment LLC (DME company)
cases.State_County: Florida (Southern District of Florida; defendants of Tamarac and Coral Springs); Virginia (Eastern District of Virginia)
cases.SchemeSummary: Defendants owned two DME companies that billed Medicare approximately $6.9 million for medically unnecessary orthotic braces, obtaining beneficiary referrals and fraudulent doctors' orders by paying kickbacks to an offshore marketing company, then laundered more than $2.2 million of the proceeds through shell companies they or their associates controlled. Forfeiture and restitution figures span three defendants (Scamarone and Mendez: $2,217,840.35 forfeiture and $3,016,324.20 restitution; Vazquez: $1,723,773.18 forfeiture and $2,249,392.09 restitution).

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of Florida
cases.FraudEntity: Marco Scamarone (owner/operator of DME companies); Jose Mendez (owner/operator of DME companies); Renee Vazquez (owner/operator of DME companies); Braces and Orthotics LLC; Stone Oak Durable Medical Equipment LLC
cases.State_County: Florida - Broward County (Tamarac, Coral Springs); Florida - Miami-Dade County (Miami); Virginia (Eastern District of Virginia)
cases.SchemeSummary: Defendants owned two durable medical equipment companies (Braces and Orthotics LLC in Virginia and Stone Oak DME LLC in Florida) that billed Medicare roughly $6.9 million for orthotic braces that were medically unnecessary and ineligible for reimbursement, obtaining beneficiary referrals and fraudulent doctors' orders by paying kickbacks and bribes to an offshore marketing company; over $2.2 million in proceeds were laundered through shell companies. All three pleaded guilty to money laundering conspiracy; Scamarone and Mendez were each ordered to pay $2,217,840.35 forfeiture and $3,016,324.20 restitution and Vazquez $1,723,773.18 forfeiture and $2,249,392.09 restitution, with sentences of 70, 78, and 60 months.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Department of Justice, Civil Division and U.S. Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of Oklahoma
cases.FraudEntity: Traditions Health LLC (home health provider)
cases.SchemeSummary: Traditions Health billed Medicare from its McAlester, Oklahoma location for home health services that were not medically necessary (2021-2024) and paid remuneration to physician-medical directors in Oklahoma and Texas who referred Medicare beneficiaries for home health services (2019-2024), potentially violating the Anti-Kickback Statute and Stark Law; the company self-disclosed and agreed to pay $34 million.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Western District of Virginia
cases.FraudEntity: Tri-Area Community Health (TACH) (Federally Qualified Health Center)
cases.State_County: Virginia - Laurel Pike (Western District of Virginia)
cases.SchemeSummary: TACH billed Medicare for Annual Wellness Visits that were performed by pharmacists without required physician supervision or presence, submitting the claims under the names of physicians who had no involvement in the visits; it agreed to pay $513,729.90, having already repaid $321,075.56.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Department of Justice, Civil Division, Commercial Litigation Branch, Fraud Section
cases.FraudEntity: Trinity Hospital Holding Company (hospital operator)
cases.SchemeSummary: Trinity allegedly rented office space from two referring physicians at rates exceeding fair market value, creating improper financial relationships, and then billed for services referred by those physicians in violation of the Stark Law; Trinity self-disclosed and settled for $1.7 million with cooperation credit.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Department of Justice, Civil Division; U.S. Attorney's Office, Middle District of Florida
cases.FraudEntity: Mark D. Fromer, P.C. d/b/a Fromer Eye Centers (ophthalmology practice); Estate of Mark Fromer (former owner of Fromer Eye Centers); Floral Park Ophthalmology P.C. (ophthalmology practice)
cases.SchemeSummary: The practices performed trans-cranial doppler ultrasounds (TCDs) on thousands of patients through a third-party testing company and billed Medicare and Medicaid hundreds of dollars per test; before results were returned, patients were labeled with a serious qualifying diagnosis that nearly none actually had, and Floral Park Ophthalmology allegedly received remuneration from the testing company to induce TCD referrals, violating the Anti-Kickback Statute and Stark Law. Fromer Eye Centers/Estate of Mark Fromer pay $1,800,000 and Floral Park Ophthalmology pays $500,000, with $384,000 going to New York's Medicaid share and a whistleblower receiving about $132,000.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of Florida
cases.FraudEntity: Kenia Marrero (organizer/purchaser and reseller of stolen patient data); Joan Navarro Bruguet (former employee of Miami-based health care provider network 'Provider A'); Juan Carlos Cardella (co-conspirator, previously sentenced on related charges)
cases.SchemeSummary: A hospital network employee photographed confidential patient records (names, DOBs, Medicare beneficiary identifier numbers) from his work computer screen and sent them via encrypted messaging to Marrero, who paid about $500 per list of ~100 beneficiaries and resold the lists for up to $7,000 each to Medicare fraudsters; over 6,000 beneficiaries' data was disclosed and Marrero also participated in a DME scheme that billed Medicare more than $5 million using the stolen identifiers, depositing over $460,000 in proceeds into the DME company's bank account.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Oregon
cases.FraudEntity: Jahangeer Ali (owner, Oregon Clinical Laboratory); Mehrdad Gerami (owner/operator, Coastal Diagnostic Testing Group and Coastal Diagnostic)
cases.PayerName: Medicare (Medicare Advantage plans); U.S. Department of Health and Human Services; Veterans Health Administration; private insurance companies
cases.SchemeSummary: Two separate defendants charged by information in one takedown announcement: Ali's Oregon Clinical Laboratory allegedly billed Medicare Advantage plans over $15 million for genetic tests that were never performed, using beneficiary and physician identifiers of people who had never heard of the lab; Gerami's Coastal Diagnostic entities allegedly billed HHS, the Veterans Health Administration and private insurers at least $2,124,363.41 for sleep studies claimed as performed in-office when they were actually done at home or not at all.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of Mississippi
cases.FraudEntity: Clint's Pharmacy; Clint Bane (former owner/operator of Clint's Pharmacy); Rommel Asagwara (owner of Lemmor Holdings, LLC d/b/a Dream Weight Clinic); Lemmor Holdings, LLC d/b/a Dream Weight Clinic
cases.SchemeSummary: Two civil complaints under the Controlled Substances Act: Clint's Pharmacy and its former owner Clint Bane could not account for 11,853 controlled substance pills found missing during on-site regulatory inspections, each pill alleged as a recordkeeping violation plus unlawful dispensing; separately, Rommel Asagwara, operating Dream Weight Clinic, allegedly negligently dispensed controlled substances outside the usual course of professional practice, failed to keep controlled substances at the registered location, and failed to maintain records/inventory for over 433,000 pills, with the United States seeking over $8 billion in civil penalties.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of Mississippi
cases.FraudEntity: Ricky Wayne Quinn (pharmacist, owner-operator of Medical Plaza at Alcorn, LLC); John Anthony "Andy" Null (pharmacist, employee of Medical Plaza Pharmacy)
cases.SchemeSummary: Two pharmacists at a Corinth, Mississippi pharmacy repeatedly billed Medicare and Medicaid multiple times for the same single dispensed prescription drug product, focusing on high-reimbursement items such as diabetic insulin pens, asthma inhalers and psychotropic medications, taking nearly $800,000. Quinn received 30 months in prison and both defendants were jointly ordered to pay $786,972.10 in restitution to Medicare.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of New York
cases.FraudEntity: Saad Aziz (owner/operator of Tri-Hamlet Taxi Inc.); Zabed Chowdhury, a/k/a 'Jared' (owner/operator of Tri-Hamlet Taxi Inc.); Tri-Hamlet Taxi Inc.
cases.State_County: New York - Suffolk County (Long Island); New York - New York City
cases.SchemeSummary: Defendants who owned Tri-Hamlet Taxi Inc. allegedly paid cash kickbacks to Medicaid beneficiaries to induce them to request ambulette transportation (mainly to methadone treatment), then billed Medicaid for trips never provided, and directed beneficiaries to request rides to distant New York City addiction treatment centers and give false pickup/drop-off addresses so they could bill for longer, higher-paying trips (over $18 million in claims for rides exceeding 75 miles; more than $35 million billed overall). Proceeds allegedly funded homes and investment properties worth about $6 million; forfeiture/restitution of at least $35 million is sought.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of Illinois
cases.FraudEntity: Burhan Mirza (organizer, resided in Pakistan); Kashif Iqbal (associated with durable medical equipment providers; money launderer); Mir Akbar Khan (recruited nominee owners); Fasiur Rahman Syed (nominee owner); Navaid Rasheed (tracked payments and disbursed proceeds)
cases.State_County: Illinois - Cook County (Chicago); Illinois - DuPage County (West Chicago); Texas - Collin County (Lavon and Plano)
cases.SchemeSummary: Defendants allegedly used nominee-owned laboratories and durable medical equipment companies to submit roughly $10 million in claims to Medicare and private insurers for items and services never provided, using stolen identifying information of patients, providers, and insurers; proceeds were laundered and transferred to Pakistan. Mirza and Iqbal are charged by indictment, while three co-schemers (Khan, Syed, Rasheed) have pleaded guilty and await sentencing.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of Illinois; U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Public Affairs
cases.FraudEntity: Burhan Mirza (organizer, Pakistani national); Kashif Iqbal (associated with durable medical equipment providers, money launderer); Mir Akbar Khan (recruiter/manager of nominee owners); Fasiur Rahman Syed (nominee owner); Navaid Rasheed (tracked fraud payments and disbursements)
cases.State_County: Illinois - Cook County (Chicago); Illinois - DuPage County (West Chicago); Texas - Collin County (Lavon, Plano)
cases.PayerName: Medicare; private health care benefit programs (private insurers)
cases.SchemeSummary: Defendants used nominee-owned laboratories and durable medical equipment companies, staffed with recruited straw owners, to submit roughly $10 million in claims to Medicare and private insurers for items and services never provided, using identifying information of patients, providers, and insurers obtained without their knowledge; proceeds were laundered and wired to Pakistan. Mirza and Iqbal are charged by indictment; three co-schemers (Khan, Syed, Rasheed) previously pleaded guilty and await sentencing.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of Georgia
cases.FraudEntity: Murrell Carnel Rutledge, Jr. (owner of Rutledge Medical Associates); Lonnie Releford (purported licensed practical nurse); Rutledge Medical Associates
cases.SchemeSummary: Rutledge, through his East Point medical practice, allegedly billed Georgia Medicaid for thousands of services never performed - nearly 900 claims for excision of complex pilonidal cysts, ~1,500 for incision and drainage of deep abscesses/hematomas, ~7,900 for extended face-to-face psychotherapy, and over 1,000 for medically unnecessary percutaneous allergy tests - seeking $4.3 million and receiving about $2.6 million. In a separate charge in the same announcement, Releford allegedly obtained nursing jobs at metro Atlanta hospitals and nursing homes by falsifying his education/credentials and stealing a real LPN's identity, causing providers to bill Medicare and Medicaid for services he was not licensed to perform; combined alleged proceeds across both defendants were $2.7 million.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of Florida
cases.FraudEntity: Michael Kochen (owner of dozens of durable medical equipment companies); Sandro Herek (director of overseas call centers)
cases.SchemeSummary: Kochen's DME companies and Herek's overseas (Egypt and other) call centers cold-called elderly Medicare Advantage beneficiaries with high-pressure telemarketing to push back, knee, shoulder and ankle braces regardless of medical necessity; physicians issued boilerplate authorizations based only on call recordings (often without speaking to the beneficiary), and Kochen paid kickbacks to telemedicine companies for the brace orders, yielding about $34 million in claims and over $17 million paid.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of Florida
cases.FraudEntity: Medical Services of America, Inc.; Traditional Home Care, Inc. d/b/a Community Home Health Services (home health providers)
cases.SchemeSummary: Home health providers allegedly paid bonuses to an employee based on the volume of Medicare patient referrals made by the employee's physician spouse, then furnished the referred designated health services and billed Medicare, in violation of the Stark Law; settlement of $702,541.20 includes $379,752 restitution, arising from a qui tam suit.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of New York
cases.FraudEntity: Elaine Antao (marketer/recruiter); Manal Wasef (marketer/recruiter); Amran Hashmi; Joseph Helmy; Amal Ismail; Zakia Khan; Seema Memon; Happy Family Social Adult Day Care Center Inc.; Family Social Adult Day Care Center Inc.; Responsible Care Staffing Inc. (home health care fiscal intermediary)
cases.SchemeSummary: Antao and Wasef acted as marketers/recruiters who referred Medicaid recipients to two Brooklyn social adult day cares and a home health fiscal intermediary in exchange for kickbacks, and paid cash bribes to beneficiaries so that over $68 million in adult day care and home health services could be billed to Medicaid though not actually provided; multiple business entities were used to launder proceeds and generate cash for the bribes. Figures span the scheme; the two defendants agreed to forfeit approximately $1 million collectively, and five others previously pleaded guilty.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Department of Justice, Criminal Division, Fraud Section; U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of New York
cases.FraudEntity: Manal Wasef (marketer/recruiter); Elaine Antao (marketer/recruiter); Happy Family Social Adult Day Care Center Inc.; Family Social Adult Day Care Center Inc.; Responsible Care Staffing Inc. (home health care fiscal intermediary)
cases.SchemeSummary: Two Brooklyn marketers/recruiters referred Medicaid recipients to two social adult day care centers and a home health fiscal intermediary in exchange for kickbacks, and paid cash bribes to the beneficiaries themselves so that over $68 million in social adult day care and home health services could be billed to Medicaid though not actually provided; multiple business entities were used to launder proceeds and generate the cash for bribes. Both defendants agreed to forfeit approximately $1 million collectively, and they are the sixth and seventh individuals to plead guilty in the case.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of New York
cases.FraudEntity: Christopher Alexander Jr. (purchaser and user of fraudulent identification documents); Devin Latrell Coleman (supplier of fraudulent identification documents)
cases.SchemeSummary: Coleman sold Alexander counterfeit driver's licenses, passport cards and Social Security cards bearing Alexander's photo with stolen victims' identifying information, and coached him via an encrypted messaging app on their use; Alexander used the documents to obtain bank loans, lines of credit and an apartment lease. Not a health care payer case - bank fraud and aggravated identity theft; restitution figures span both defendants ($30,500 for Alexander plus a $15,000 forfeiture judgment, with Coleman liable for $15,000 jointly and severally).

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Western District of Pennsylvania
cases.FraudEntity: Abdou Jallow (convenience store manager); Alicia Mastrantoni (store employee)
cases.PayerName: U.S. Department of Agriculture - Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP)
cases.SchemeSummary: Jallow, the manager of a Pittsburgh convenience store, and Mastrantoni, an employee, allegedly exchanged customers' SNAP food-stamp benefits for cash (which many customers used to buy illegal drugs), concealing the transactions by entering fraudulent UPC codes on the store register; over $550,000 in SNAP benefits were allegedly trafficked. Charged by criminal complaint as part of the 2026 National Health Care Fraud Takedown.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of New York; U.S. Department of Justice, Criminal Division, Fraud Section
cases.FraudEntity: Inwoo Kim, aka 'Tony Kim' and 'Long Jin' (owner of pharmacy and two social adult day care centers - Z & W Empire Enterprise Inc. d/b/a Royal Adult Daycare and Happy Life Inc.); Daniel Lee, aka 'Daniel Yang' and 'Donghee Yang' (program director at Happy Life)
cases.State_County: New York - Queens County (Flushing); New York - Kings County (Brooklyn)
cases.SchemeSummary: Defendants allegedly paid cash and supermarket gift certificates to Medicare beneficiaries and Medicaid recipients to induce them to fill prescriptions at Kim's pharmacy and to enroll at his social adult day care centers, then billed Medicare and Medicaid roughly $120 million for prescription drugs and day care services that were medically unnecessary, never provided, or induced by kickbacks - including day care claims exceeding the centers' permitted capacity. Cash for the bribes was withdrawn from bank accounts they controlled.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Department of Justice, National Fraud Enforcement Division (Criminal Division, Fraud Section)
cases.FraudEntity: Reyad Salahaldeen (controlled four laboratories); Mohamad Mustafa (co-owner/controller of Express Diagnostics and BioConfirm); Express Diagnostics, LLC; BioConfirm Laboratory USA, LLC; BioConfirm Laboratories, LLC; Tox Management, LLC; Tri-State Toxicology, LLC; Travores Wills (marketer); Elijua Watson (marketer); Diego Pancha Valencia (marketer); Shauntae Walker (nurse practitioner); Cassandra Latham (nurse practitioner); LaTosha McCune (marketer); Vinit Patel (physician); Jose Rodriguez Ospina (physician); Edward Giles (marketer); Derek McCune (marketer); Nelson Giraldo (physician)
cases.PayerName: Medicare; Medicaid; private health insurance companies
cases.SchemeSummary: Salahaldeen and Mustafa paid kickbacks and bribes to 'marketers' who solicited Medicare, Medicaid and privately insured beneficiaries by telemarketing, door-to-door and health fairs to collect insurance information and DNA swabs, then paid providers who never treated the patients to sign laboratory requisition forms for expensive cancer/pharmacogenetic tests; the four labs billed about $522 million and were paid about $84 million, with sham marketing contracts, invoices, falsified requisitions and letters of medical necessity used to disguise the kickbacks. Figures and sentences span both sentenced defendants plus eleven previously sentenced co-conspirators (longest of those, 46 months).

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Massachusetts
cases.FraudEntity: Heriberto Rodriguez; Mirian Chalas; Santo Escolastico Cuello; John Doe (identity unknown, Quincy, Mass.); John Doe (identity unknown); John Doe (identity unknown, Lynn, Mass.); John Doe (identity unknown); Mario Baez Romero; Richard Odelis Vallegas Nunez; Miguel Diaz Matos; Mitul Patel; Santo Tejada Sanchez; Jennifer Ferran; Owen Landry a/k/a 'Oski'; Yahaira Diaz Gomez
cases.State_County: Massachusetts - Framingham; Worcester; Quincy; Somerville; Allston (Boston); Lynn; Haverhill; Mattapan (Boston); New Hampshire - Salem
cases.PayerName: MassHealth (Massachusetts Medicaid); SNAP (USDA); Social Security Administration; HUD; state unemployment benefits
cases.SchemeSummary: Fifteen defendants, most alleged to be in the U.S. illegally and several living under stolen identities, allegedly submitted false statements and fraudulent applications - often using stolen Social Security numbers and fraudulent identification/passport documents - to enroll in and collect MassHealth (Medicaid), SNAP, Social Security disability, HUD housing and unemployment benefits for which they were ineligible, totaling more than $1.4 million across all defendants (individual MassHealth losses ranged from about $32,717 to $266,000). One defendant is charged in a related scheme staging a fake armed robbery so participants could claim U Visas as crime victims.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Massachusetts
cases.FraudEntity: Teva Pharmaceuticals; Raytheon Company; Insys Therapeutics (founder and six former executives)
cases.SchemeSummary: Fiscal Year 2025 collections roundup: the District of Massachusetts entered settlements exceeding $900 million, including a $425 million resolution with Teva Pharmaceuticals for paying kickbacks through two co-pay assistance foundations in violation of the Anti-Kickback Statute and False Claims Act (largest co-pay assistance settlement to date), and a $575 million criminal/civil resolution with Raytheon over defense contract fraud; the office also completed collection of $48,344,036 in criminal restitution for victims of the Insys Therapeutics health care racketeering conspiracy. Figures span multiple defendants and cases.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of New Mexico
cases.SchemeSummary: Not a health care fraud case: weekly immigration enforcement statistics for the District of New Mexico (illegal reentry, alien smuggling, illegal entry charges), including an alien-smuggling case involving a tractor trailer stopped at the Las Cruces checkpoint. Health care fraud is mentioned only as a prior conviction category for some illegal-reentry defendants; no payer, scheme, or amount is described.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Middle District of Tennessee
cases.FraudEntity: Pitts Therapies, LLC d/b/a Cornerstone Pediatric Therapies (pediatric therapy clinic)
cases.SchemeSummary: Pediatric therapy clinic allegedly billed TRICARE for two units of a billing code per day per beneficiary when only one unit per day was allowed (2020 through October 2022), and billed two separate codes for services where only one code was payable ('unbundling') from 2020 through mid-2025; settled for $300,000 with no determination of liability.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of New York
cases.FraudEntity: Dr. Robert Simon (New Jersey-based urologist); Dr. Nicole Fleischmann (New York-based urologist)
cases.SchemeSummary: Two urologists billed Medicare for permanent implantations of InterStim sacral nerve stimulators without completing the preoperative percutaneous nerve evaluation testing and voiding diaries required by NCD 230.18, and implanted two devices bilaterally in the same procedure without justification; Simon additionally falsely documented successful PNE results, performed unnecessary battery/device replacement and revision surgeries, and double-billed Medicare for lead removal. Combined settlement of $1,112,695.88 (Simon) and $1,101,044.80 (Fleischmann) plus interest resolved a whistleblower False Claims Act suit joined by the government.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Pennsylvania
cases.FraudEntity: Michael Glickert (chiropractor); Joseph Novof (physician, Medical Director); The Vanguard Clinic LLC (integrated chiropractic clinic); Fleur de Lis, LLC (Sanexas device distributorship)
cases.SchemeSummary: United States filed a False Claims Act complaint alleging that a chiropractor developed and promoted nationwide a scheme to bill Medicare for RST-Sanexas neoGEN electrical nerve stimulation treatments and accompanying vitamin injections that are not reimbursable when furnished in outpatient clinics for pain, supplying coding instructions to other providers; the clinic's medical director falsely certified the vitamin injections as medically necessary without even knowing their ingredients, and billing continued after the defendants admitted the services were not covered.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of New York
cases.SchemeSummary: Document is a personnel announcement naming new leadership for the U.S. Attorney's Office Long Island Division; it describes no specific charged fraud case, only referencing in passing a past healthcare/wire fraud conviction handled by an appointee.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Massachusetts
cases.FraudEntity: Fifteen unnamed individuals charged since December 2025, including nine individuals charged on March 26, 2026 (one a Dominican national)
cases.SchemeSummary: Announcement of a new Benefit and Voter Fraud Team; the office has charged 15 individuals with nearly $9 million in benefit fraud since December 2025, including nine defendants charged the same day for allegedly using stolen identities to collect nearly $300,000 in SNAP, Social Security and MassHealth benefits. Cases were developed from recipient data analysis showing the same identities drawing benefits simultaneously in two or more states/territories (e.g., roughly 495 identities receiving Massachusetts DTA SNAP benefits while also receiving SNAP in Puerto Rico in December 2024).

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of West Virginia
cases.FraudEntity: Raymond C. "Rocky" Meadows II (founder and director, Lifehouse Inc.); Helen Crutcher Meadows (collector supervisor, Lifehouse Inc.); West Virginia Sleep Centers, LLC (sleep laboratory)
cases.State_County: West Virginia - Cabell County (Huntington); West Virginia - Raleigh County (Beckley)
cases.PayerName: Medicaid (West Virginia); Veterans Administration Community Health program
cases.SchemeSummary: Two separate matters announced together: Raymond and Helen Meadows were charged by criminal complaint with conspiracy to commit wire fraud for falsifying and submitting timesheets to a drug-testing laboratory for drug testing work never performed at Lifehouse Inc., a sober living program - including routinely billing 32 hours of overtime per week and hours logged while on out-of-state vacations - with the laboratory paying on those timesheets and then obtaining reimbursement from federal and state health care programs. Separately, West Virginia Sleep Centers LLC paid $120,000 to settle allegations it billed Medicaid and the VA Community Health program from January 1, 2016 through January 9, 2020 for sleep studies and polysomnogram reports prepared and signed by unqualified non-physician staff.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of New Jersey
cases.SchemeSummary: Not a fraud case: personnel announcement of the appointment of Joyce M. Malliet as First Assistant U.S. Attorney for the District of New Jersey.

cases.JurisdictionName: South Dakota Attorney General's Office (with U.S. Attorney's Office, District of South Dakota)
cases.FraudEntity: Sharon Monson (owner, At Home Nursing)
cases.SchemeSummary: Sharon Monson, owner of At Home Nursing in Pierre, was indicted on five state felony counts for allegedly defrauding the South Dakota Medicaid Program of roughly $588,000, with charges of unlawful receipt of medical benefits, aggravated grand theft, perjury, and failure to maintain necessary records; the release does not describe the billing mechanics. This case is one of several federal and state fraud matters summarized in a joint press conference release, but it is the only health care payer case.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Virginia
cases.FraudEntity: Jair Barbour (qualified mental health provider); Mikia Noble (Chief Operating Officer, Advancing Communities Everywhere); Abdul Rehman Sirhandi (straw owner, Pulse Medical Supply)
cases.State_County: Virginia - Henrico County; Virginia - Chesterfield County (North Chesterfield); Virginia - Loudoun County (Aldie)
cases.SchemeSummary: Three separate EDVA defendants charged as part of the 2026 national takedown: Barbour allegedly submitted hundreds of falsified progress notes for mental health sessions that never occurred and overstated hours worked, billing Virginia Medicaid $345,670.93; Noble, COO of Advancing Communities Everywhere, allegedly conspired to bill approximately $49.6 million (about $38.6 million paid) in crisis mental health claims for low-income and homeless Medicaid recipients who never received or did not need the services; Sirhandi allegedly served as straw owner of DME company Pulse Medical Supply and conspired with others in Texas and Pakistan to submit about $780,627 in false Medicare claims, of which about $313,233 was paid. Figures span three defendants.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Missouri
cases.FraudEntity: Michael McCormac (former owner of a mail order pharmacy)
cases.SchemeSummary: In an annual collections announcement, the office reported recovering $1,323,318 from Michael McCormac, a former mail order pharmacy owner who pleaded guilty to two Anti-Kickback Statute counts for paying kickbacks to marketing companies to generate prescriptions for expensive medications billed to Medicare and the Missouri and Ohio Medicaid programs. The release separately notes about $2.9 million collected in an unrelated disability fraud case involving two Jefferson County chiropractors and more than two dozen patients.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Florida
cases.FraudEntity: Israel Guardarrama
cases.SchemeSummary: In a fiscal year 2025 debt-collection summary, the office reported that Israel Guardarrama was convicted of conspiracy to commit health care fraud and wire fraud and ordered to pay $1,722,080.27 in restitution; $1.4 million was recovered through a criminal restitution judgment lien foreclosure action against his homestead and rental properties. The document gives no detail on the billing mechanics or payer. (The same release also lists non-health-care collections against Issa Asad/Q Link Wireless and Michael Scott Segal.)

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Western District of Virginia
cases.FraudEntity: Duane Dixon (former doctor)
cases.SchemeSummary: Annual district collections announcement reporting $10,621,656.97 collected in FY2025; it notes $200,000 collected from the conviction of former doctor Duane Dixon, who concealed health care fraud and prescribed highly addictive opioid painkillers to at-risk patients at pain clinics in Central and Southwest Virginia. No billing mechanics or payer are described.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Maine
cases.FraudEntity: SVCMC Inc., formerly known as Saint Vincents Catholic Medical Centers of New York
cases.PayerName: U.S. Department of Defense (healthcare for retired military members and their families)
cases.SchemeSummary: As part of a January 2025 False Claims Act agreement, SVCMC Inc. paid $29 million to resolve allegations that it knowingly retained erroneously inflated payments it received from the Department of Defense for healthcare services provided to retired military members and their families; the payment was among $29,563,154.06 collected jointly with other DOJ components in FY2025 reported by the District of Maine.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Middle District of Florida
cases.FraudEntity: Leigh Tesar (nurse practitioner); Walter Presha, Jr. (nurse); Koby Evans (nurse); Leo Corrigan (corporation owner); Konstantin Braverman (kickback middleman); Lawrence Waldman (former sales representative, ASAP Labs); Rustam Abdaev (operator of Sunny and Recovery Inc.); Henry Garcia (owner, New Level 3 and On-Point Medical Alliance); Marc Vincent Pazienza (attorney); Laurent Cassagnol (VA employee); Heriberto L. Rivera (CEO, Family Integrative Medicine of Orlando, LLC)
cases.State_County: Florida - Sarasota County (Sarasota); Florida - Manatee County (Ellenton, Bradenton); Florida - Hillsborough County (Tampa, Apollo Beach); Florida - Palm Beach County (Lake Worth); Florida - Miami-Dade County (Miami); Florida - Pasco County; Florida - Orange County; Florida - Lake County
cases.PayerName: Medicare; Medicare Advantage (Medicare Part C); Florida Medicaid; TRICARE; U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs
cases.SchemeSummary: Combined Middle District of Florida takedown covering multiple schemes: nurse practitioner Tesar billed Medicare over $118 million in 18 months (about $61 million paid) for medically unnecessary or never-applied skin allografts and wound care on patients referred by nurses Presha and Evans in exchange for kickbacks; Corrigan bought Medicare beneficiary ID numbers to bill over $7.5 million for unrequested OTC COVID-19 tests and sold beneficiary data to labs for genetic testing, taking $1.7 million in kickbacks; Braverman brokered marketer lists of beneficiary data to providers who shipped unrequested COVID-19 tests, causing about 152,000 claims and $14.4 million in Medicare reimbursements with $1.5 million to him; Waldman paid kickbacks from ASAP Labs to physicians to sign requisitions for unnecessary genetic and respiratory tests billed to Medicare, Medicaid and TRICARE (pleaded guilty; $5 million FCA civil settlement); Abdaev used Sunny and Recovery Inc. plus stolen beneficiary and physician identifiers to bill Medicare Part C and Florida Medicaid over $19 million for DME braces never provided ($941,000 paid) and wired proceeds abroad; Garcia's DME companies used offshore call centers and sham telehealth physician orders to bill Medicare Advantage for unneeded braces, paying kickbacks per reimbursed order; Rivera paid VA employee Cassagnol about $175,172 to steer VA patients to FIMO, generating about $14 million in VA claims ($11.9 million paid); attorney Pazienza stole over $300,000 of clients' Medicare-fraud proceeds he claimed to safeguard and produced false documents to a grand jury. Figures span multiple defendants and schemes.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Nevada
cases.SchemeSummary: Not a case: press release announcing a Health Care Fraud Consortium Workshop hosted by the U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of Nevada with HHS-OIG, FBI, IRS-CI, and the DOJ Criminal Division Fraud Section, discussing fraud trends, the West Coast Health Care Fraud Strike Force, and the Corporate Whistleblower Awards Pilot Program. No defendant, scheme, or loss amount is described.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of Ohio
cases.FraudEntity: MP Lab Solutions, LLC
cases.SchemeSummary: The USAO and HHS-OIG settled allegations that MP Lab Solutions, LLC of Highland Heights, Ohio submitted false claims to Medicare for over-the-counter COVID-19 test kits; the company paid the $200,000 settlement in full. (Document is a quarterly collections release; other listed matters were non-health-care cases.)

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Missouri
cases.FraudEntity: Jonathan Wayne Morris (physician, clinic owner)
cases.SchemeSummary: Indictment alleges the physician billed Medicare and Missouri Medicaid for clinic services falsely listing himself as the rendering provider when the services were actually performed by assistant physicians (medical school graduates requiring supervision), and caused claims for controlled substance prescriptions issued outside the usual course of professional practice, including to patients with substance use disorders and individuals with whom he had sexual relations.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Department of Justice, Criminal Division (Violent Crime and Racketeering Section) and U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Kansas
cases.FraudEntity: Newton Jones (former President, International Brotherhood of Boilermakers); Kateryna Jones (spouse of Newton Jones, union employee); William Creeden (former Secretary Treasurer); Lawrence McManamon (former Vice President)
cases.State_County: Kansas; North Carolina - Chapel Hill (Orange County); Missouri - Kearney; Ohio - Rocky River
cases.PayerName: Boilermakers Union health and welfare benefit plan (private employee benefit plan)
cases.SchemeSummary: Union officers were convicted of RICO, embezzlement, wire fraud and health care fraud for looting Boilermakers Union dues over roughly 15 years - over $5 million in luxury foreign travel, nearly $2 million in salary/benefits for no-show jobs (including ~$1.8 million to Newton Jones's wife), over $160,000 in personal restaurant charges, unearned vacation payouts, theft from the union retirement plan, and a $7 million unauthorized union loan to the Bank of Labor where two defendants held paid positions. The health care fraud count involved unearned health benefits provided through the union plan to Kateryna Jones, charged against Newton Jones, Kateryna Jones and Creeden; figures span multiple defendants and no separate health care fraud loss amount was stated.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of New York
cases.FraudEntity: Community Care Health Network, LLC d/b/a Matrix Medical Network (health services company performing in-home assessments for Medicare Advantage Organizations)
cases.State_County: Tennessee - Nashville (headquarters); New York - New York County (Southern District of New York)
cases.PayerName: Medicare (Medicare Advantage / Part C, via Medicare Advantage Organizations and CMS)
cases.SchemeSummary: Matrix conducted nurse-practitioner in-home 'health assessments' of Medicare Advantage members (paid $350-$450 per assessment by 30+ MAOs) and reported risk-adjusting diagnosis codes - proliferative diabetic retinopathy, drug-induced and rheumatoid polyneuropathy, atrial fibrillation, rheumatoid arthritis, COPD, and simple chronic bronchitis - that lacked supporting clinical information or diagnostic testing and were not reported by any treating provider, so the MAOs received inflated risk-adjusted capitated payments from CMS; a related whistleblower FCA suit was joined and Matrix entered a five-year Corporate Integrity Agreement.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of Illinois
cases.FraudEntity: Amirali Bhimani (seller of Medicare beneficiary information); Daniel Robinson (Founder and CEO of ODA Solutions, Inc.); ODA Solutions, Inc.
cases.SchemeSummary: Two separate Chicago-area defendants charged in one announcement: Bhimani allegedly sold Medicare beneficiary information to laboratories that billed Medicare roughly $342 million (about $240 million paid) for over-the-counter Covid-19 test kits beneficiaries never requested or received, supplying labs with AI-generated fake recordings of beneficiaries purportedly consenting; Robinson allegedly directed staff at his company ODA Solutions to create fake medical records and bill Illinois Medicaid over $92 million (about $75 million paid) for behavioral health counseling never provided, including for deceased beneficiaries, then moved ~$45 million into brokerage/business accounts and spent over $7 million on real estate, vehicles, jewelry and a yacht. Figures span both defendants.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Rhode Island
cases.SchemeSummary: Not a fraud case: this document is a personnel announcement naming the leadership team of the U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of Rhode Island. No scheme, defendant, payer, or loss amount is described.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Middle District of Pennsylvania
cases.SchemeSummary: Not a fraud case: the document is an administrative announcement that Brian D. Miller was reappointed by the U.S. District Court to continue as United States Attorney for the Middle District of Pennsylvania. No fraud scheme, defendant, payer, or amount is described.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Middle District of Pennsylvania
cases.FraudEntity: Eye Consultants of Pennsylvania, PC (ophthalmology practice); Florentina Mayko (chief executive officer of medical clinics)
cases.SchemeSummary: Annual collections release listing two Medicare matters: Eye Consultants of Pennsylvania, PC paid $790,000 to resolve False Claims Act allegations that it billed Medicare for Evaluation & Management services in violation of Medicare rules; and Florentina Mayko, CEO of medical clinics, conspired to defraud Medicare by billing for medically unnecessary urine drug tests on chronic opioid patients, and was ordered to pay $1,409,076.48 in restitution plus forfeiture of several properties (figures span two separate defendants).

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Western District of New York
cases.FraudEntity: Pfizer Inc.; Biohaven (Pfizer subsidiary)
cases.SchemeSummary: Year-end roundup announcing the Affirmative Civil Enforcement Unit recovered over $68 million in 2025, of which the principal health care matter was a False Claims Act settlement in which Pfizer, on behalf of its subsidiary Biohaven, paid more than $50 million to resolve allegations that Biohaven paid kickbacks to providers to induce them to prescribe its migraine drug Nurtec. The remaining recoveries included five Paycheck Protection Program fraud cases totaling more than $10 million and self-disclosed overpayments to federal health care programs.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of West Virginia
cases.FraudEntity: Four unnamed labor organizations (PPP loan recipients)
cases.State_County: West Virginia - Northern District of West Virginia
cases.SchemeSummary: Aggregate annual report of the Affirmative Civil Enforcement Unit, which recovered $5,324,902 in FY2025 (over $250 million since 2003) under the False Claims Act and Controlled Substances Act; the largest single FY2025 settlement was approximately $5.1 million paid by four labor organizations alleged to have applied for and obtained COVID-19 Paycheck Protection Program loans they knew or should have known they were ineligible to receive. No specific health care fraud scheme is described.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of New Mexico
cases.FraudEntity: Rick Q. Wilson, aka Henry Quintero (psychologist/prescriber)
cases.SchemeSummary: Civil complaint alleges a New Mexico psychologist issued more than 21,000 controlled substance prescriptions between 2017 and 2020 - high-dose benzodiazepines such as Xanax combined with other CNS depressants like Ambien - without legitimate medical purpose, using repetitive unsupported diagnoses, no individualized treatment plans or drug screening/PMP checks, while accepting primarily cash payments; the government seeks civil penalties for each unlawful prescription.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Middle District of Florida
cases.FraudEntity: Dr. Kevin Rosenbach (allergy and immunology physician); Kevin P. Rosenbach, M.D. P.A.
cases.SchemeSummary: The civil complaint alleges the physician changed or added a rare immunodeficiency disease diagnosis to patient records for patients who did not meet the disease definition, so that subcutaneous immune globulin therapy would be covered; specialty pharmacies dispensing the immune globulins then submitted the resulting false claims to Medicare Part B, causing over $1.9 million in losses.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Nebraska; U.S. District Court for the District of Nebraska
cases.FraudEntity: Joan Kicken (pharmacist, owner and operator); AME P.C. d/b/a Campbell Drug (pharmacy)
cases.SchemeSummary: Pharmacist and her pharmacy allegedly billed Medicaid for prescription drugs that were never dispensed and for drugs lacking any valid prescription, and billed Medicare and Medicaid for higher-reimbursing name-brand medications while actually dispensing generic versions; a default judgment of $3,423,389.84 was entered under the False Claims Act after defendants failed to defend.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of West Virginia (with U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of West Virginia)
cases.FraudEntity: West Virginia United Health System, Inc., d/b/a West Virginia University Health System (WVUHS) (hospital system)
cases.SchemeSummary: Following a DEA investigation, WVUHS agreed to pay $4,177,139 and enter a three-year Memorandum of Agreement to resolve civil allegations of Controlled Substances Act violations between 2017 and 2024, including failing to notify DEA of thefts or significant losses of controlled substances, errors in controlled substance orders, inaccurate inventory records, improper authority for use of DEA order forms, and noncompliant policies and procedures across registered facilities.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Central District of California
cases.FraudEntity: Expert Wound Care PC (Pasadena-based advanced wound care clinic)
cases.SchemeSummary: Clinic submitted more than $46.6 million in Medicare claims for skin substitute grafts, skin grafts and application procedures purportedly provided to 78 beneficiaries, receiving about $34 million; investigators found at least one beneficiary billed $2.6 million (52 graft applications, 27 December claims) never received any skin grafts or home services. The government obtained a seizure warrant for approximately $2,039,792 from the clinic's bank account.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Massachusetts
cases.FraudEntity: Dr. Alexandria Williams (physician who signed DME orders); Integrated Support Plus, Inc. (telemedicine company)
cases.SchemeSummary: Civil False Claims Act complaint alleges a doctor signed pre-populated orthotic brace orders generated from telemarketing calls to Medicare beneficiaries she never examined, falsely certifying she had evaluated the patients and discussed/instructed on orthotic use; she was paid per order reviewed via a staffing company connected to a telemedicine firm, and DME suppliers used the orders to bill Medicare roughly $630,000 for unnecessary braces.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Utah
cases.FraudEntity: Ryan Scott Ellsworth (podiatrist, owner of Summit Foot and Ankle and Amble Medical); Emily Kelly (nurse practitioner); Drake Dell Broadbent (registered nurse); Summit Foot and Ankle; Amble Medical
cases.State_County: Utah - Washington County (St. George); Utah - Utah County (Highland)
cases.SchemeSummary: A podiatrist and two nurses allegedly billed Medicare for skin substitute applications on patients who lacked qualifying wounds and where the treatment was medically unnecessary, ignoring the requirement of 30 days of prior basic wound care; they routinely waived/never pursued large beneficiary copayments to keep patients coming, and Ellsworth allowed an unqualified nurse (Broadbent) to perform skin substitute services outside his scope while billing them under Ellsworth's own name and Medicare provider number. Ellsworth billed $44 million (Medicare paid over $19 million) and Kelly billed $17 million (over $10 million paid), with Medicare paying about $29 million in total.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Department of Justice, Civil Division and U.S. Attorney's Office, Central District of California
cases.FraudEntity: Serrano Kidney & Vascular Access Center (physician practice); Dr. Feliciano Serrano (physician)
cases.SchemeSummary: Dr. Serrano allegedly billed Medicare and California Medicaid for medically unnecessary dialysis access interventions (angioplasty/stents) and peripheral artery disease interventions (stents/atherectomies) on 20 beneficiaries, routinely repeating procedures every few days, weeks or months without clinical benefit; he overstated the degree of stenosis and falsely documented patient symptoms and conservative therapy in medical records to make the procedures appear justified. Settlement totals over $6.73 million: nearly $6.51 million to the United States and nearly $229,000 to California, with a qui tam relator receiving about $976,000.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Massachusetts
cases.FraudEntity: Veloxis Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (drug manufacturer)
cases.State_County: North Carolina - Cary (company headquarters); Massachusetts (district of prosecution)
cases.SchemeSummary: Veloxis paid transplant health care professionals lavish meals, alcohol, luxury resort stays, personal gifts and sham consulting fees, and paid specialty pharmacies per-patient/per-month fees disguised in contracts as 'enhanced services,' to induce prescriptions and purchases of its kidney transplant drug Envarsus XR, causing false claims to Medicare, Medicaid and TRICARE; employees falsified expense reports to conceal the payments and evade Open Payments (Sunshine Act) reporting. Resolution comprised a $10.04M criminal penalty under a three-year DPA, $34.45M False Claims Act civil settlement ($21,211,251 federal / $13,238,749 states) and a $1.55M CMS civil penalty.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Department of Justice, Civil Division and U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Massachusetts
cases.FraudEntity: Veloxis Pharmaceuticals Inc. (drug manufacturer)
cases.SchemeSummary: Veloxis, the maker of the kidney transplant immunosuppressant Envarsus XR, paid kickbacks to transplant health care providers (lavish dinners, alcohol, gifts, luxury resort trips styled as 'advisory boards', and sham consulting fees for work never performed) and per-patient/per-month payments to specialty pharmacies disguised in contracts as 'enhanced services' data/adherence fees, to induce prescriptions and purchases over a cheaper generic; the resulting Envarsus claims were billed to Medicare, Medicaid and TRICARE, and employees falsified expense reports to hide attendees and conceal payments, causing underreporting to CMS's Open Payments (Sunshine Act) program. Resolution: deferred prosecution agreement with a criminal penalty over $10 million, $21,211,251 to the United States and $13,238,749 to states under the False Claims Act, and a $1.55 million Sunshine Act civil penalty, plus a five-year Corporate Integrity Agreement.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Central District of Illinois
cases.FraudEntity: Howard Keith Wilson (sole owner, Wilson's Body Shop)
cases.SchemeSummary: Wilson, sole owner of a collision repair shop, withheld federal employment taxes (including Social Security and Medicare withholdings) from employees' pay via Forms W-2 from 2013 through 2020 but never remitted them or the employer's share to the IRS ($351,152 loss), and failed to file personal income tax returns for 2018-2020 despite substantial income ($505,871 additional loss). No health care payer was billed; the case is tax fraud.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Virginia
cases.FraudEntity: Divine Youth Counseling, LLC (mental health agency); E'mon Ambers; Armone' Ambers; TraQuan Brown; T'Aisya Squire
cases.SchemeSummary: Divine Youth Counseling billed Medicaid more than $11 million for Crisis Stabilization and Mobile Crisis mental health services, falsely claiming two mental health professionals simultaneously provided 'Team Treatment' when at most one was present; the coconspirators also paid over $470,000 in kickbacks by buying hotel rooms for Medicaid recipients to induce them to obtain services from the agency, with proceeds laundered through monetary transactions. Charges cover four defendants; three await a May 2026 jury trial and one (Squire, false statements) is set to plead guilty.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of New York
cases.FraudEntity: Dr. Douglas Cline (physician, owner/operator of Chronic Pain Management); Laurie McKenna (nurse practitioner)
cases.State_County: New York - Warren County (Queensbury; Bolton Landing)
cases.SchemeSummary: Cline ran a cash-pay pain practice (Chronic Pain Management) in Queensbury, NY where hundreds of patients, including a combat-wounded TRICARE beneficiary and his spouse, received escalating high-dose opioid and benzodiazepine prescriptions tied to recurring appointment fees, often without being examined in person by any provider; after the federal investigation began Cline transferred a lake house worth over $1 million to his ex-wife, prompting a separate fraudulent conveyance action. The two defendants jointly agreed to pay $500,000 and are barred from DEA registration for 20 years.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Massachusetts
cases.FraudEntity: EyePoint, Inc., formerly EyePoint Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (pharmaceutical manufacturer)
cases.SchemeSummary: EyePoint allegedly induced ambulatory surgery centers to purchase and dispense its drug DEXYCU by (1) an 'Assurance Program' that reimbursed ASCs in cash or free replacement product when federal insurers denied coverage, and (2) giving thousands of free DEXYCU samples used on commercially insured patients whose insurers would not pay, eliminating ASCs' financial risk and driving DEXYCU claims billed to Medicare, Medicaid and TRICARE; resolved for $4,678,981 federal plus $25,478 to participating states, with a five-year Corporate Integrity Agreement and $791,768.74 to the qui tam relator.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Wisconsin
cases.FraudEntity: Kinex Medical Company, LLC (durable medical equipment supplier)
cases.PayerName: Medicare; TRICARE; Federal Employees Health Benefits Program (FEHBP); Office of Workers Compensation Programs (U.S. Department of Labor)
cases.SchemeSummary: Kinex allegedly supplied knee, shoulder and hip braces that patients did not need and billed Medicare, TRICARE, FEHBP and OWCP as if medically necessary, inducing patients to accept the braces by waiving co-pays and giving free additional equipment; resolved via a $6.925 million False Claims Act settlement and a Corporate Integrity Agreement following a qui tam complaint.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Western District of Missouri
cases.FraudEntity: Syed Makki (government imposter wire fraud conspiracy participant/gold bar courier); Amanda Rutherford (purported caregiver); Peter A. Lee (attorney)
cases.State_County: Missouri - Jackson County (Kansas City); Missouri - Clay County; Missouri - Cedar County (Stockton); Kansas - Geary County (Junction City)
cases.SchemeSummary: General World Elder Abuse Awareness Day announcement summarizing several unrelated elder-fraud prosecutions rather than a health care billing scheme: Syed Makki was sentenced to 15.5 years for a government-imposter wire fraud conspiracy collecting gold bars from elderly victims; Amanda Rutherford got 6 years for stealing firearms and collector coins from an elderly couple she claimed to care for; attorney Peter A. Lee pleaded guilty to wire fraud after taking $296,140 in client funds from decedent estates and a special needs trust between January 2019 and February 2025; the office also seized $1.2 million in digital currency and over $325,000 in cryptocurrency tied to online investment scams targeting older victims.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Western District of Oklahoma
cases.FraudEntity: Stewart Johnson (operator, Combined Home Medical Equipment); Stephen Johnson (operator, Combined Home Medical Equipment); Combined Home Medical Equipment (durable medical equipment company); Judy Dennis (licensed speech-language pathologist)
cases.State_County: Oklahoma - Comanche County (Lawton); Oklahoma - Oklahoma County (Oklahoma City)
cases.SchemeSummary: Two separate matters announced together: the Johnsons, who ran DME company Combined Home Medical Equipment supplying CPAP machines, allegedly submitted claims to TRICARE for more than 650,000 in-person CPAP-related services that were never provided and that they were not qualified to provide, collecting over $27 million (2018-2024); separately, speech-language pathologist Judy Dennis was sued civilly under the federal and Oklahoma False Claims Acts for more than $2.5 million in claims to Medicare, Oklahoma Medicaid and TRICARE for speech-language pathology services not rendered, not medically necessary, or non-compliant with program requirements. FraudAmt combines both matters.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of Indiana
cases.FraudEntity: Shayna Williams (individual)
cases.State_County: Indiana - Hamilton County (Westfield); Indiana - Marion County (Indianapolis)
